title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
summary: Garlic, chili and good olive oil. Quick, spicy, unbeatable.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it generously.
steps.tip: Salty like the sea, that's what makes pasta taste great.

steps.text: Peel the garlic and slice it thinly. Deseed the chili and chop it finely. Chop the parsley.
Add the spaghetti to the boiling water and cook until al dente.
steps.label: Cook spaghetti

steps.text: Meanwhile, gently warm the olive oil in a large pan over low heat. Let the garlic and chili turn lightly golden.
steps.tip: Not too hot! Burnt garlic turns bitter.

steps.text: Scoop out a cup of pasta water. Then drain the spaghetti and add it straight to the pan.
Toss with a splash of pasta water and the parsley until everything is glossy. Serve with Parmesan.
steps.tip: The pasta water makes the sauce silky.

title: Tomato Mozzarella Pasta
summary: Fruity tomato sauce with melting mozzarella and basil.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Halve the cherry tomatoes, finely chop the garlic and dice the mozzarella.
Add the penne to the boiling water and cook until al dente.
steps.label: Cook penne

steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a pan. Briefly fry the garlic, then add the cherry tomatoes and fry them too.
steps.label: Fry tomatoes

steps.text: Pour in the passata, season with salt, pepper and a pinch of sugar and let it simmer.
steps.tip: The pinch of sugar takes the edge off the tomatoes' acidity.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Drain the pasta and mix it into the sauce. Fold in the mozzarella and basil leaves, let it melt briefly and serve.

title: Chili sin Carne
summary: Spicy bean chili with corn and bell pepper, no meat needed.

steps.text: Finely chop the onion and garlic. Deseed and dice the bell pepper.
Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion until translucent. Briefly fry the garlic with it.
steps.label: Sauté onion

steps.text: Add the bell pepper and tomato paste, toast briefly and stir in the spices.
steps.tip: Toasting the spices briefly wakes up their aroma.

steps.text: Pour in the tomatoes and stock, bring to a boil and simmer with the lid on.
steps.label: Simmer chili

steps.text: Rinse the beans and corn in a sieve, drain and add them to the chili. Keep simmering.
steps.label: Simmer beans & corn

steps.text: Season with salt and pepper. Serve with a dollop of sour cream and baguette.

title: Chili con Carne
summary: The classic with ground beef, beans and plenty of spice.

steps.text: Finely chop the onion and garlic. Deseed and dice the bell pepper.
Heat the oil in a large pot until very hot and brown the ground beef, breaking it up.
steps.tip: Don't stir too often, that's how the beef gets nice and browned.
steps.label: Brown beef

steps.text: Add the onion, garlic and bell pepper and fry them too.
steps.label: Fry vegetables

steps.text: Stir in the tomato paste and spices and toast briefly.
Pour in the tomatoes and stock, bring to a boil and simmer with the lid on.
steps.label: Simmer chili

steps.text: Rinse and drain the beans and corn and add them. Keep simmering.
steps.label: Simmer beans & corn

steps.text: Season with salt and pepper and serve with sour cream and baguette.

title: Vegetable Coconut Curry
summary: Creamy red curry with sweet potato and broccoli.

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the amount of water and a little salt, then let it steam covered on low heat.
steps.tip: Keep the lid on, that makes the rice nice and fluffy.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Peel and dice the sweet potato. Cut the broccoli into florets and the bell pepper into strips. Finely chop the onion and ginger.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the onion and ginger. Add the curry paste and toast it for a minute.
Add the sweet potato, coconut milk and 100 ml water and let it simmer.
steps.label: Simmer sweet potato

steps.text: Add the broccoli and bell pepper and keep simmering until everything is tender.
steps.label: Simmer vegetables

steps.text: Season with soy sauce and lime juice and serve with the rice.

title: Chicken Curry
summary: Tender chicken in a mild coconut curry sauce with peas.

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the amount of water and a little salt, then let it steam covered on low heat.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Finely chop the onion, garlic and ginger.
Heat the oil in a pan and brown the chicken on all sides.
steps.label: Brown chicken

steps.text: Add the onion, garlic and ginger, stir in the curry powder and tomato paste and toast briefly.
Add the coconut milk and peas and simmer gently.
steps.tip: Only a gentle simmer, that keeps the chicken juicy.
steps.label: Simmer curry

steps.text: Season with salt and serve with the rice.

title: Shakshuka
summary: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, with warm flatbread.

steps.text: Dice the onion and bell pepper, finely chop the garlic.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and cook the onion and pepper until soft.
steps.label: Sauté vegetables

steps.text: Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and fry for one minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes, season with salt and pepper and let it reduce.
steps.label: Reduce sauce

steps.text: Use a spoon to make four wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and let them set.
steps.tip: The whites should be firm, the yolks can stay runny.
steps.label: Set eggs

steps.text: Crumble the feta on top, sprinkle with parsley and eat straight from the pan with flatbread.

title: Potato Leek Soup
summary: Creamy, warming, cozy. Perfect for cold days.

steps.text: Peel and dice the potatoes. Halve the leek lengthwise, wash it thoroughly and slice into rings. Dice the onion.
Melt the butter in a pot and sauté the onion and leek.
steps.label: Sauté leek

steps.text: Add the potatoes and stock, bring to a boil and simmer with the lid on until the potatoes are soft.
steps.label: Simmer soup

steps.text: Blend the soup and stir in the cream.
steps.tip: Set aside a few leek rings beforehand and use them as garnish, it looks lovely.

steps.text: Season with salt, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg.
Snip the chives, sprinkle over the soup and serve with bread rolls.

title: Roast Vegetables with Feta
summary: Colorful sheet-pan veggies with potatoes and creamy feta.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (fan).
Wash and halve the potatoes. Cut the zucchini, bell pepper and onion into large chunks.
Toss the potatoes with half the oil, salt and herbs on a baking tray and put them in the oven.
steps.tip: The potatoes need longer, so they get a head start.
steps.label: Potatoes in oven

steps.text: Toss the remaining vegetables and cherry tomatoes with the rest of the oil, salt and pepper and add them to the tray.
Crumble the feta on top and bake everything until done.
steps.label: Bake feta

steps.text: Let it cool for a moment and serve straight from the tray.

title: Spaghetti Bolognese
summary: Slow-simmered meat sauce, just like grandma's.

steps.text: Dice the onion, carrot, celery and garlic very finely.
Heat the oil in a pot and brown the ground meat, breaking it up.
steps.label: Brown mince

steps.text: Add the vegetables and fry them too.
steps.label: Fry vegetables

steps.text: Toast the tomato paste briefly, then add the passata, oregano, salt, pepper and a pinch of sugar.
Let the sauce simmer over low heat with the lid on. Stir now and then.
steps.tip: The longer the sauce simmers, the better it gets.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Meanwhile, bring salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
steps.label: Cook spaghetti

steps.text: Drain the spaghetti, serve with the sauce and freshly grated Parmesan.

title: Cheese Spätzle
summary: Swabian soul food with mountain cheese and crispy onions.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (fan).
Slice the onions into thin rings and fry them in half the butter over medium heat until golden. Set aside.
steps.tip: Patience pays off: slowly fried onions turn sweet and crispy.
steps.label: Fry onions

steps.text: Add the remaining butter to the pan and warm the spätzle in it.
steps.label: Warm spätzle

steps.text: Layer spätzle and cheese alternately in a baking dish, peppering each layer.
Bake until the cheese has melted.
steps.label: Bake

steps.text: Sprinkle with the fried onions and chives and serve hot.

title: Mushroom Risotto
summary: Creamy risotto with fried mushrooms and Parmesan.

steps.text: Heat the stock in a small pot and keep it warm.
Slice the mushrooms, finely dice the onion and garlic.
Heat the oil in a pot until very hot and sear the mushrooms. Season with salt and pepper and set aside.
steps.label: Fry mushrooms

steps.text: Add half the butter to the pot and sauté the onion and garlic until translucent. Add the rice and toast it until glassy.
Add a ladle of stock and stir until absorbed. Keep going until the rice is creamy and al dente.
steps.tip: Only add more once the rice has almost soaked up the stock.
steps.label: Stir risotto

steps.text: Stir in the mushrooms, Parmesan and remaining butter, let rest for two minutes and serve with parsley.

title: Salmon with Roast Potatoes
summary: Juicy oven-baked salmon with crispy potatoes and dill dip.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (fan).
Wash and quarter the potatoes, toss with oil and salt and roast them on a tray.
steps.label: Potatoes in oven

steps.text: For the dip, chop the dill and stir it with the quark, a little lemon juice, salt, pepper and a splash of water until creamy.
steps.tip: A splash of water makes the quark nice and creamy.

steps.text: Salt the salmon, place it on the tray next to the potatoes, top with lemon slices and bake.
steps.tip: The salmon is perfect when it's still slightly translucent inside.
steps.label: Salmon in oven

steps.text: Plate everything and serve with the dill dip.

title: Gnocchi with Spinach
summary: Crispy gnocchi with tomatoes, spinach and cream cheese. Ready in 20 minutes.

steps.text: Halve the cherry tomatoes and finely chop the garlic.
Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the gnocchi until golden.
steps.tip: Don't flip them too often, that's how they get crispy.
steps.label: Fry gnocchi

steps.text: Add the tomatoes and garlic and fry them too.
steps.label: Fry tomatoes

steps.text: Add the spinach and let it wilt. Stir in the cream cheese and a splash of water.
Season with salt and pepper and serve sprinkled with Parmesan.

title: Red Lentil Dal
summary: Warming Indian lentil dish with coconut milk and spinach.

steps.text: Finely chop the onion, garlic and ginger. Rinse the lentils in a sieve.
Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion until translucent.
steps.label: Sauté onion

steps.text: Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and turmeric and toast for one minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, coconut milk and stock. Bring to a boil and simmer, stirring now and then.
steps.tip: Red lentils fall apart while cooking, that's exactly how it should be.
steps.label: Simmer dal

steps.text: Stir in the spinach, season with lime juice and salt and serve with flatbread.

title: Chicken Wraps
summary: Crunchy wraps with spiced chicken, salad and cheese.

steps.text: Cut the chicken into thin strips and season with paprika, salt and pepper.
Shred the lettuce, dice the tomatoes and cucumber.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the chicken strips until cooked through.
steps.label: Fry chicken

steps.text: Warm the wraps one by one in a dry pan for a few seconds on each side.
Spread the wraps with yogurt and top with lettuce, vegetables, chicken and cheese.
steps.tip: Don't overfill, or it'll be hard to roll.

steps.text: Fold in the sides, roll up tightly, cut in half and enjoy.

title: Fried Potatoes with Fried Eggs
summary: Crispy German fried potatoes with onions and a fried egg. Simply good.

steps.text: Parboil the potatoes in their skins in salted water.
steps.tip: Potatoes from the day before are ideal. Parboiling works too.
steps.label: Par-boil potatoes

steps.text: Drain, let cool briefly, peel and slice. Dice the onion.
Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the potatoes in a single layer. Only flip once they're crispy underneath.
steps.tip: Don't flip too early, the crust needs time.
steps.label: Fry potatoes

steps.text: Add the onion, season with salt, pepper and paprika and keep frying.
steps.label: Fry with onion

steps.text: Melt the butter in a second pan and crack in the eggs. Fry over medium heat.
steps.label: Fried eggs

steps.text: Serve the potatoes with the fried eggs and sprinkle with chives.

title: Pancakes
summary: Golden German pancakes with apple sauce and cinnamon sugar. Sweet happiness.

steps.text: Whisk the flour, milk, eggs, 1 tbsp sugar and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter.
Let the batter rest briefly.
steps.tip: Resting makes the pancakes nice and fluffy.
steps.label: Rest batter

steps.text: Mix the remaining sugar with the cinnamon.
Melt a little butter in a pan over medium heat, add a thin layer of batter, cook until golden, then flip.
steps.tip: When the edge comes loose, it's time to flip.
steps.label: Fry pancakes

steps.text: Repeat until all the batter is used.
Serve with apple sauce and cinnamon sugar.

title: Stuffed Peppers
summary: Peppers filled with ground beef and rice, baked in tomato sauce.

steps.text: Parboil the rice in salted water and drain.
steps.label: Par-cook rice

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (fan). Cut a lid off each pepper and remove the seeds. Finely dice the onion.
Heat the oil in a pan and brown the ground beef with the onion, breaking it up.
steps.label: Brown mince

steps.text: Mix the meat with the rice, paprika, salt and pepper and fill the peppers.
Put the passata with oregano, salt and pepper in a baking dish, set the peppers in, put the lids on and bake.
steps.label: Peppers in oven

steps.text: Remove the lids, sprinkle cheese over the filling and bake until golden.
steps.label: Bake cheese

steps.text: Serve with the tomato sauce from the dish.

title: Asian Stir-Fry Noodles
summary: Stir-fried egg noodles with crunchy vegetables and soy sauce.

steps.text: Cook the noodles according to the package, drain and rinse with cold water.
steps.label: Cook noodles

steps.text: Cut the carrots and bell pepper into thin strips, slice the mushrooms and the spring onions. Finely chop the garlic and ginger.
Get a large pan or wok very hot. Add the oil, then stir-fry the carrots, pepper and mushrooms.
steps.tip: High heat and constant stirring keep the vegetables crunchy.
steps.label: Stir-fry veg

steps.text: Add the garlic, ginger and spring onions and fry for one minute.
Add the noodles, soy sauce, sesame oil and honey and toss everything well.
steps.label: Toss noodles

steps.text: Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve right away.

title: Flammkuchen
summary: Wafer-thin Alsatian tart with crème fraîche, bacon and onions.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C (top and bottom heat).
steps.tip: It needs to be really hot, that's what makes the base crispy.

steps.text: Unroll the dough with its baking paper onto a tray.
Stir the crème fraîche with salt, pepper and a little nutmeg and spread it thinly over the dough.
Slice the onion into thin rings and scatter it over the dough together with the bacon.
Bake until the edge is golden and crispy.
steps.label: Bake tarte flambée

steps.text: Cut into pieces and serve hot.

title: Couscous Salad with Halloumi
summary: Fresh salad with chickpeas, vegetables and fried halloumi.

steps.text: Bring the stock to a boil, pour it over the couscous and let it soak, covered.
steps.label: Soak couscous

steps.text: Chop the cucumber, tomatoes and onion. Rinse and drain the chickpeas. Chop the parsley.
For the dressing, whisk lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and mix with the vegetables, chickpeas, parsley and dressing.
steps.tip: Fluffing with a fork keeps it from clumping.

steps.text: Slice the halloumi and fry it in a dry pan until golden on both sides.
steps.label: Fry halloumi

steps.text: Plate the salad and top it with the warm halloumi.

title: Pumpkin Soup
summary: Velvety Hokkaido soup with ginger, coconut milk and toasted seeds.

steps.text: Wash the pumpkin, halve it, scoop out the seeds and dice the flesh.
steps.tip: With Hokkaido you can simply eat the skin.

steps.text: Peel and chop the onion, carrot and ginger.
Heat the oil in a large pot, sauté the onion, carrot and ginger and briefly toast the curry powder.
steps.label: Sauté vegetables

steps.text: Add the pumpkin and stock, bring to a boil and simmer with the lid on until everything is soft.
steps.label: Simmer soup

steps.text: Add the coconut milk, blend until smooth and season with salt and pepper.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan, sprinkle over the soup and serve with baguette.

title: Honey Soy Chicken Stir-Fry
summary: Chicken and vegetables in a sweet and salty honey soy glaze with rice.

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the amount of water and a little salt, then let it steam covered on low heat.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Dice the chicken. Dice the zucchini and bell pepper, slice the onion, chop the garlic.
Heat the oil in a large pan and brown the chicken on all sides. Set aside.
steps.label: Brown chicken

steps.text: Add the vegetables to the pan and fry until tender-crisp.
steps.label: Fry vegetables

steps.text: Return the chicken to the pan. Add the soy sauce, honey and garlic and glaze everything.
steps.tip: Honey caramelizes fast, so keep stirring.
steps.label: Glaze

steps.text: Season with pepper and serve with the rice.

title: Homemade Burgers
summary: Juicy beef patties with cheddar and all the trimmings.

steps.text: Knead the ground beef with salt and pepper and shape two flat patties. Press a small dent into the middle.
steps.tip: The dent stops the patties from puffing up while frying.

steps.text: Slice the tomato, onion and pickles, wash the lettuce leaves.
Heat the oil in a pan until very hot and fry the patties on the first side.
steps.label: Patties side 1

steps.text: Flip the patties, put a slice of cheddar on each, cover and finish cooking.
steps.label: Patties side 2

steps.text: Cut the buns open and toast the cut sides briefly in the pan.
Spread the buns with ketchup and mayo and stack with lettuce, patty, tomato, onion and pickles.

title: Tagliatelle with Creamy Salmon
summary: Creamy lemon sauce with smoked salmon and dill.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Add the tagliatelle to the boiling water and cook until al dente.
steps.label: Cook tagliatelle

steps.text: Meanwhile, finely dice the shallot and sauté it in butter until translucent.
Add the cream and a little grated lemon zest and let it reduce slightly.
steps.label: Reduce sauce

steps.text: Cut the salmon into strips, chop the dill and add both to the sauce.
steps.tip: Don't cook the salmon anymore, just warm it. That keeps it tender.

steps.text: Drain the pasta, toss with the sauce and season with lemon juice and pepper.

title: Creamy Tortellini
summary: Tortellini with ham and peas in a creamy Parmesan sauce.

steps.text: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil.
Finely dice the onion, cut the ham into strips.
Melt the butter in a pan and fry the onion and ham.
steps.label: Fry ham

steps.text: Add the cream and peas and simmer gently. Season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Add the tortellini to the boiling water and cook according to the package.
steps.label: Cook tortellini

steps.text: Drain the tortellini, add them to the sauce, stir in the Parmesan and serve.

title: Ratatouille
summary: French vegetable stew with herbes de Provence.

steps.text: Cut the eggplant, zucchini, bell peppers and onion into bite-sized cubes. Chop the garlic.
Heat half the oil in a large pot and fry the eggplant.
steps.tip: Eggplant soaks up a lot of oil, that's normal.
steps.label: Fry eggplant

steps.text: Add the remaining oil, onion, garlic and bell peppers and fry them too.
steps.label: Fry peppers

steps.text: Add the zucchini, tomatoes and herbs, season with salt and pepper and braise with the lid on.
steps.label: Braise ratatouille

steps.text: Season to taste and serve with fresh baguette.

title: Meatballs with Mashed Potatoes
summary: Old-school German comfort food: juicy meat patties and creamy mash.

steps.text: Soak the bread roll in a bowl of water.
Peel and quarter the potatoes and boil them in salted water until soft.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Finely dice the onion. Squeeze the bread roll out well.
Knead the meat, bread, egg, onion, mustard, salt and pepper and shape six patties.
steps.tip: With wet hands nothing sticks.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the patties over medium heat on all sides until cooked through.
steps.label: Fry meatballs

steps.text: Drain the potatoes and mash them with warm milk, butter, salt and nutmeg.
Serve the patties with the mash.

title: Egg Fried Rice
summary: Asian-style fried rice with vegetables, egg and spring onions.

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the amount of water and a little salt, let it steam covered, then spread it on a plate to cool.
steps.tip: Rice from the day before is ideal, fresh rice is stickier.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Finely dice the carrot, slice the spring onions, chop the garlic.
Heat a little oil in a large pan, whisk the eggs, pour them in and scramble. Set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the pan and fry the carrot, peas and garlic.
steps.label: Fry vegetables

steps.text: Add the rice and fry over high heat.
steps.tip: Leave it alone for a bit, then it gets slightly crispy underneath.
steps.label: Fry rice

steps.text: Mix in the egg, soy sauce, sesame oil and spring onions and serve.

title: Asparagus with Hollandaise
summary: White asparagus, new potatoes and a hollandaise that never splits.

steps.text: Wash the potatoes and boil them in their skins in salted water.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Peel the asparagus starting just below the tip and working down, then cut off the woody ends.
steps.tip: Don't throw away the peels and ends! They give the cooking water extra asparagus flavor.

steps.text: In a wide pot, bring water to a boil with 1 tsp salt, the sugar, a knob of butter and a slice of lemon. Simmer the peels and ends in it, then fish them out.
steps.label: Simmer peels

steps.text: Lay the asparagus in the gently simmering water and cook until it bends slightly when you lift it.
steps.tip: Thick spears need a bit longer. The bend test tells you.
steps.label: Cook asparagus

steps.text: For the hollandaise, heat the remaining butter in a small pot until it foams and is really hot.

Put 3 egg yolks, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp water and a pinch of salt in a tall cup. Place an immersion blender at the bottom, switch it on and pour in the hot butter in a thin stream until the sauce is thick and creamy.
steps.tip: The trick: the hot butter cooks the yolks and the blender holds everything together. Works every time!

steps.text: Plate the asparagus and potatoes, pour over the hollandaise and sprinkle with chives.

title: Frankfurt Green Sauce
summary: The Hessian Easter classic: seven herbs, sour cream, eggs and jacket potatoes.

steps.text: Wash the potatoes and boil them in their skins in salted water.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Hard-boil the eggs, rinse them in cold water and peel.
steps.label: Boil eggs

steps.text: Wash the herbs, shake them dry and remove thick stems. Then chop them very finely.
steps.tip: The seven herbs are borage, chervil, cress, parsley, salad burnet, sorrel and chives. In spring you can buy them bundled!

steps.text: Halve two eggs, press the yolks through a sieve and stir them smooth with mustard, vinegar, oil, salt and pepper.
steps.tip: The mashed yolk makes the sauce extra creamy, almost like a light mayonnaise.

steps.text: Stir in the schmand and sour cream, then add the herbs. Chop the whites of the two eggs and fold them in.
Let the sauce sit for a bit and season it boldly.
steps.label: Let sauce sit

steps.text: Peel the potatoes and serve with the green sauce and the remaining eggs, halved.

title: Wild Garlic Pesto Pasta
summary: Fresh wild garlic pesto with toasted pine nuts. Tastes like spring.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden.
steps.tip: Keep an eye on them! Pine nuts go from golden to burnt in seconds.
steps.label: Toast pine nuts

steps.text: Wash the wild garlic, pat it dry and chop roughly.
steps.tip: Real wild garlic smells clearly of garlic when you rub it. That's how you know it's the right thing.

steps.text: Blend the wild garlic, half the pine nuts, grated Parmesan, olive oil, a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt into a pesto.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente.
steps.label: Cook spaghetti

steps.text: Save a cup of pasta water, drain the pasta and toss it in the pot with the pesto and a splash of pasta water. Serve with the remaining pine nuts.
steps.tip: Don't heat the pesto, or the wild garlic loses its color and aroma.

title: Lamb Chops with Rosemary Potatoes
summary: Rosy lamb chops, crispy rosemary potatoes and green beans. Perfect for Easter.

steps.text: Take the lamb chops out of the fridge. Preheat the oven to 220 °C (fan).
steps.tip: Meat at room temperature cooks much more evenly.

steps.text: Halve the potatoes, toss them with 2 tbsp olive oil, salt, rosemary needles and crushed garlic cloves and roast on a tray.
steps.tip: Cut side down, that's how they get really crispy.
steps.label: Potatoes in oven

steps.text: Trim the beans and cook them in salted water until just tender, then rinse in cold water.
steps.label: Cook beans

steps.text: Pat the chops dry and salt them.
Heat the remaining oil in a pan until very hot and fry the chops for 2 to 3 minutes per side.
steps.label: Fry chops

steps.text: Add the butter, a rosemary sprig and a garlic clove to the pan and baste the meat with the foaming butter. Then let it rest briefly.
steps.tip: Resting is a must: that keeps the juices in the meat instead of on the plate.
steps.label: Baste & rest

steps.text: Toss the beans briefly in the pan butter. Serve everything with pepper and a little lemon zest.

title: Mustard Eggs with Mashed Potatoes
summary: A German grandma classic and the best use for leftover Easter eggs.

steps.text: Peel and dice the potatoes and boil them in salted water until soft.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Boil the eggs, rinse them in cold water and peel.
steps.tip: At 9 minutes the yolk is set but still moist, not grey.
steps.label: Boil eggs

steps.text: Finely dice the onion. Melt 2 tbsp butter in a pot and sauté the onion until translucent. Dust with the flour and cook briefly.
steps.label: Sauté onion

steps.text: Gradually stir in the stock and 150 ml milk and simmer until the sauce thickens.
steps.tip: Add the liquid gradually and you won't get lumps.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Stir in the mustard and season with salt, pepper and a pinch of sugar. Halve the eggs and place them in the sauce.
Drain the potatoes, let them steam dry briefly, mash with the remaining milk and butter and season with nutmeg.
steps.tip: Warm the milk first and the mash gets extra fluffy.

steps.text: Serve the mash with the mustard eggs and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Gazpacho
summary: Ice-cold Spanish tomato soup. The best excuse not to cook on hot days.

steps.text: Roughly chop the tomatoes. Peel the cucumber, deseed the pepper and roughly dice both. Peel the shallot and garlic. Finely dice a little cucumber and pepper for the topping and set aside.
Mix the vegetables with the bread, 1 tsp salt and the vinegar in a bowl and let it sit.
steps.tip: The salt draws juice out of the vegetables. That makes the soup much more intense.
steps.label: Let veg sit

steps.text: Blend everything finely while slowly pouring in the olive oil until the soup turns creamy.
steps.tip: The oil makes the gazpacho velvety, almost like an emulsion.

steps.text: Season and chill for at least an hour.
steps.label: Chill

steps.text: Pour into bowls, scatter over the diced vegetables and finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Panzanella
summary: Tuscan bread salad with sun-ripened tomatoes, toasted bread and burrata.

steps.text: Cut the tomatoes into chunks, put them in a sieve over a bowl, salt them and let them drain.
steps.tip: Don't pour away the tomato juice you catch. It goes into the dressing!
steps.label: Drain tomatoes

steps.text: Tear the ciabatta into cubes, toss with 2 tbsp olive oil and toast in a pan until golden.
steps.label: Toast bread

steps.text: Slice the cucumber and cut the red onion into thin rings.
Whisk the tomato juice with the vinegar, remaining olive oil, salt and pepper into a dressing.
Toss the bread, tomatoes, cucumber, onion and basil with the dressing and let it sit briefly.
steps.tip: 10 minutes is enough: the bread soaks up the juices but stays crisp at the edges.
steps.label: Let salad sit

steps.text: Tear the burrata open and serve it on top of the salad.

title: Pasta alla Norma
summary: Sicilian classic with fried eggplant, tomato sauce and ricotta.

steps.text: Dice the eggplants, toss with 1 tsp salt and let them sit in a sieve.
steps.tip: The salt draws out water, so the eggplant soaks up less oil and turns lovely and creamy.
steps.label: Salt eggplant

steps.text: Pat the eggplant dry and fry in hot olive oil until golden all over. Remove from the pan.
steps.label: Fry eggplant

steps.text: Slice the garlic and fry briefly in the remaining oil. Add the chili and tomatoes and simmer.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Meanwhile, cook the rigatoni in salted water until al dente.
steps.label: Cook rigatoni

steps.text: Add the eggplant and basil to the sauce. Add the pasta with a splash of pasta water and toss.
Serve with dollops of ricotta and basil.

title: Zucchini Fritters with Yogurt Dip
summary: Crispy fritters with feta and mint, plus a fresh garlic yogurt.

steps.text: Coarsely grate the zucchini, mix with 1 tsp salt and let it sit.
steps.label: Salt zucchini

steps.text: Squeeze the zucchini hard in a clean kitchen towel until hardly any liquid comes out.
steps.tip: This is the secret! The drier the zucchini, the crispier the fritters.

steps.text: Slice the spring onions, chop the mint and crumble the feta. Mix half the mint with the spring onions, feta, egg, flour and pepper into the zucchini.
Stir the yogurt with grated garlic, a little lemon juice, salt and the remaining mint.
Heat the oil in a pan, add a tablespoon of batter per fritter, flatten and fry until golden on both sides.
steps.tip: Only flip when the edge turns golden.
steps.label: Fry fritters

steps.text: Drain the fritters briefly on paper towels and serve with the dip.

title: Chicken Souvlaki with Tzatziki
summary: Lemony marinated skewers, creamy tzatziki and warm pita.

steps.text: Cut the chicken into large cubes. Marinate with the juice and zest of the lemon, 2 grated garlic cloves, oregano, 3 tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper.
steps.tip: No longer than a few hours, or the lemon makes the meat mealy.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.text: For the tzatziki, coarsely grate the cucumber, salt it and squeeze it well.
steps.tip: Squeezed cucumber means creamy tzatziki instead of a watery puddle.

steps.text: Stir the cucumber with the yogurt, 1 grated garlic clove, 1 tbsp olive oil and salt.
Slice the tomatoes and red onion. Thread the meat onto the skewers.
Cook the skewers in a grill pan or on the grill until cooked through and browned.
steps.label: Grill skewers

steps.text: Warm the pita briefly in the pan. Serve with the skewers, tzatziki, tomatoes and onion.

title: Esquites (Mexican Street Corn Salad)
summary: Charred corn with lime, chili, feta and cilantro. Street food by the spoonful.

steps.text: Cut the kernels off the cobs with a sharp knife.
Heat the oil in a large pan until very hot. Add the corn and let it char without stirring until it blackens in spots.
steps.tip: Don't stir! The charred bits bring grill flavor without a grill.
steps.label: Char corn

steps.text: Finely chop the spring onions, chili and garlic, add to the corn and toast briefly.
steps.label: Toast aromatics

steps.text: Transfer the corn to a bowl and let it cool a little.
Stir in the mayonnaise, sour cream, lime juice, paprika and salt.
Crumble the feta over the top and sprinkle with cilantro. Tortilla chips go great with it.

title: Tagliatelle with Chanterelles
summary: Chanterelles fried in butter, with cream, parsley and Parmesan.

steps.text: Clean the chanterelles dry: brush off the soil with a brush or paper towel and halve large ones.
steps.tip: Don't wash them! They soak up water and turn mushy in the pan.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Finely dice the shallots.
Fry the chanterelles in a large dry pan over high heat until their water has evaporated.
steps.tip: Dry-fry first, then add butter: that makes them flavorful instead of rubbery.
steps.label: Fry chanterelles

steps.text: Add the butter and shallots and fry until golden. Season with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Fry with butter

steps.text: Cook the tagliatelle until al dente.
steps.label: Cook tagliatelle

steps.text: Pour the cream over the mushrooms and reduce briefly. Add the pasta with a splash of pasta water and fold in the Parmesan.
Serve with parsley and a squeeze of lemon.

title: German Onion Tart
summary: Juicy onion tart from the tray with bacon and caraway. Traditionally with a glass of young wine!

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and 1 tsp salt. Add the lukewarm milk and 2 tbsp oil and knead into a smooth dough. Cover and let it rise.
steps.tip: A warm spot, like near the heater, makes the dough rise faster.
steps.label: Let dough rise

steps.text: Meanwhile, halve the onions and cut them into thin strips.
Render the bacon in a large pot. Add the butter and onions and sweat over medium heat until soft and translucent, not brown.
steps.tip: Be patient: slowly sweated onions turn sweet and mild.
steps.label: Sweat onions

steps.text: Let the onions cool a little. Stir in the schmand and eggs and season boldly with caraway, nutmeg, salt and pepper. Preheat the oven to 200 °C (top/bottom heat).
Roll the dough out thinly on an oiled tray and pull up the edges a little. Spread the onion mixture on top.
Bake until golden brown.
steps.label: Bake onion tart

steps.text: Let it cool briefly and serve lukewarm.
steps.tip: It tastes best lukewarm, and it cuts more cleanly.

title: Pumpkin Pasta with Sage Butter
summary: Roasted Hokkaido squash, nutty brown butter and crispy sage.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C (fan). Deseed the squash and cut it, skin on, into 2 cm cubes.
steps.tip: No need to peel Hokkaido, the skin turns completely soft in the oven.

steps.text: Toss the squash with olive oil, salt and pepper and roast on the tray until browned at the edges.
steps.label: Squash in oven

steps.text: Cook the pasta in salted water until al dente.
steps.label: Cook pasta

steps.text: Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat until it smells nutty and turns brown. Fry the sage leaves and garlic in it until crispy.
steps.tip: Brown butter smells like hazelnuts. As soon as it's golden brown, take it off the heat!
steps.label: Sage butter

steps.text: Mash half the squash with a little pasta water into a cream. Add the pasta, squash cream, squash cubes and Parmesan to the pan and toss.
Serve with nutmeg, a squeeze of lemon and chopped walnuts.

title: Potato Pancakes with Applesauce
summary: Rhineland potato pancakes: crispy outside, juicy inside, with homemade applesauce.

steps.text: Peel and dice the apples and simmer until soft with the sugar, cinnamon, a squeeze of lemon and 3 tbsp water. Then mash roughly.
steps.label: Simmer applesauce

steps.text: Peel the potatoes and finely grate them together with the onion.
Squeeze the mixture hard in a kitchen towel, catching the liquid. Let it stand briefly, pour off the liquid and add the white starch from the bottom back to the batter.
steps.tip: Pro trick: the settled potato starch holds the pancakes together, no flour needed.

steps.text: Mix in the eggs, oats and 1 tsp salt.
Heat plenty of oil in a pan. Add two tablespoons of batter per pancake, flatten and fry until crispy on both sides.
steps.tip: Lots of hot oil and thin pancakes make the edges really crunchy.
steps.label: Fry pancakes

steps.text: Drain on paper towels and serve right away with the applesauce.

title: Beef Goulash
summary: Hungarian-inspired: almost as many onions as meat and two hours of patience.

steps.text: Halve the onions and cut them into strips, chop the garlic and dice the bell pepper. Pat the meat dry and cut large pieces down to about 3 cm.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the meat well in two batches. Remove.
steps.tip: Don't crowd the pot, or the meat stews in its own juices instead of browning.
steps.label: Brown meat

steps.text: Add the onions to the pot and cook over medium heat until golden brown.
steps.tip: The onions break down completely later and thicken the sauce without any flour.
steps.label: Cook onions

steps.text: Briefly toast the garlic and tomato paste. Take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika.
steps.tip: Never keep frying paprika in hot fat, it turns bitter quickly.

steps.text: Add the meat, bell pepper, stock, caraway, marjoram and bay leaves. Bring to a boil and braise covered over low heat.
steps.label: Braise goulash

steps.text: Remove the lid and keep braising until the meat is tender and the sauce is thick.
steps.label: Braise uncovered

steps.text: Season with vinegar, salt and pepper. Serve with noodles, spätzle or fresh bread.

title: Cabbage Rolls
summary: White cabbage leaves with a savory mince filling, braised in gravy. A real grandma classic.

steps.text: Cut out the core in a wedge. Put the cabbage head in boiling salted water and peel off the outer leaves one by one as they soften. You need 8 to 12 large leaves.
steps.tip: Pro shortcut: freeze the whole cabbage overnight. Once thawed, the leaves come off super easily!
steps.label: Blanch cabbage

steps.text: Drain the leaves and shave the thick center rib flat.
Soak the bread roll in water and squeeze it out. Finely dice the onion and chop the parsley. Knead with the meat, egg, mustard, paprika, salt and pepper.
Overlap 2 leaves, place a portion of filling on top, fold in the sides and roll up tightly. Wrap each roll with a slice of bacon.
Heat the oil in a casserole and brown the rolls all over.
steps.label: Brown rolls

steps.text: Briefly toast the tomato paste, deglaze with the stock, add the caraway and braise covered.
steps.tip: Baste them with the gravy now and then to keep them juicy.
steps.label: Braise rolls

steps.text: Remove the rolls, stir the cream into the gravy and season. Serve with boiled potatoes or mash.

title: Tartiflette
summary: Savoyard potato bake with bacon, onions and a whole Reblochon. Pure winter joy.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water until almost done, drain and let them cool a little.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (top/bottom heat). Peel and slice the potatoes. Cut the onion into strips.
Render the bacon in a pan until crispy. Add the onions and fry until soft.
steps.label: Bacon & onions

steps.text: Deglaze with the white wine and reduce until it has almost evaporated.
steps.label: Reduce wine

steps.text: Rub a baking dish with the halved garlic clove. Mix the potatoes with the bacon and onions and the crème fraîche, fill the dish and season with pepper.
steps.tip: Rubbing the dish with garlic is an old Savoyard trick: subtle flavor without sharp bits.

steps.text: Halve the Reblochon horizontally and place it rind side up on the potatoes. Bake until the cheese melts and turns golden.
steps.label: Bake tartiflette

steps.text: Serve with a crisp green salad and a tangy vinaigrette.

title: Kale with Smoked Sausage
summary: Northern German winter classic with caramelized potatoes. Best after the first frost.

steps.text: Strip the kale off the thick stems and wash thoroughly. Blanch briefly in boiling salted water and chop roughly.
steps.tip: Wash thoroughly: sand likes to hide in the curly leaves.
steps.label: Blanch kale

steps.text: Dice the onion and sauté it in 1 tbsp clarified butter in a large pot until translucent.
Add the kale and stock and braise covered over low heat.
steps.label: Braise kale

steps.text: Lay the sausages on top of the kale and let them cook with it. They give their flavor to the kale.
steps.label: Cook sausages

steps.text: Peel the potatoes and boil them in salted water. Then caramelize them in a pan with the remaining clarified butter and the sugar until golden.
steps.tip: Sweet glazed potatoes are a must with kale in northern Germany!
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Stir the oats into the kale and keep simmering. Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
steps.tip: Oats bind the kale and make it wonderfully creamy. An old grandma recipe.
steps.label: Simmer kale

steps.text: Serve the kale with the sausages, the potatoes and a dollop of mustard.

title: Königsberg Meatballs
summary: Tender meatballs in a creamy caper sauce with boiled potatoes.

steps.text: Soak the bread roll and squeeze it out. Dice the onion very finely. Finely chop the anchovies.
Knead the meat with the bread, onion, anchovies, 1 egg, salt and pepper and shape into 8 to 10 balls.
steps.tip: You won't taste the anchovies, but they add exactly the savoriness that makes the original.

steps.text: Bring the stock to a boil with the bay leaf, lower the heat and let the meatballs poach in it. Don't let it bubble!
steps.label: Poach meatballs

steps.text: Peel the potatoes and boil them in salted water.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Remove the meatballs. Melt the butter in a pot, cook the flour in it briefly and gradually whisk in 500 ml of the stock.
Stir in the cream and capers and simmer. Take off the heat, stir in 1 egg yolk and season with lemon juice.
steps.tip: Add the yolk at the very end and don't boil it again, or it will curdle.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Warm the meatballs in the sauce and serve with the potatoes.

title: Split Pea Soup with Sausages
summary: Hearty German pea soup, just like from the field kitchen, with frankfurters.

steps.text: Dice the onion. Clean and chop the soup vegetables. Peel and dice the potatoes.
Render the bacon with the oil in a large pot, add the onion and soup vegetables and sweat them.
steps.label: Bacon & veg

steps.text: Rinse the peas in a sieve and add them with the stock and bay leaf. Let it simmer.
steps.tip: Split peas don't need soaking. Just rinse and go!
steps.label: Simmer peas

steps.text: Add the potatoes and marjoram and keep simmering until the peas fall apart.
steps.tip: Stir now and then, peas like to stick to the bottom.
steps.label: Simmer soup

steps.text: Remove the bay leaf. Mash the soup a little with a potato masher to make it nice and creamy.
Slice the frankfurters and heat them in the soup. Don't boil any more, or they burst.
steps.label: Heat sausages

steps.text: Season with salt and pepper and serve. It tastes even better the next day!

title: Potato Salad with Sausages
summary: The German Christmas Eve classic: Swabian potato salad made with broth, silky and lukewarm.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water until just tender.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Meanwhile, dice the onion very finely and bring it to a boil with the stock. Stir in the vinegar, mustard, sugar, salt and pepper.
Drain the potatoes, let them steam dry briefly, peel while still warm and slice thinly.
steps.tip: They have to be warm! Only warm potatoes really soak up the broth.

steps.text: Pour the hot onion broth over the potatoes, mix gently and let it soak in.
steps.tip: Don't be afraid of a little mush: in Swabia the salad should be 'schlotzig', silky and glossy.
steps.label: Let salad soak

steps.text: Fold in the oil. Thinly slice the cucumber and mix it in with the chives. Taste again, it usually needs a bit more vinegar or broth.
Warm the frankfurters in hot, not boiling, water.
steps.label: Warm sausages

steps.text: Serve the lukewarm potato salad with the sausages. Merry Christmas!

title: Beef Roulades with Red Cabbage
summary: The ultimate German holiday dinner: roulades with mustard, bacon and pickle in a dark gravy.

steps.text: Cut two onions into strips and quarter the pickles lengthwise. Roughly dice the remaining onion, the carrot and the celeriac.
Lay the beef slices flat, season with salt and pepper and spread thinly with mustard. Top with bacon, onion strips and pickle, fold in the sides, roll up tightly and pin.
steps.tip: Folding in the sides matters: it keeps the filling inside while braising.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a casserole until very hot and brown the roulades dark all over. Remove.
steps.tip: The darker the browning, the better the gravy. Patience pays off here!
steps.label: Brown roulades

steps.text: Toast the diced vegetables in the casserole, add the tomato paste and toast until it sticks slightly to the bottom.
steps.label: Toast vegetables

steps.text: Deglaze with the red wine and reduce almost completely. Add the stock and bay leaves, return the roulades and braise covered.
steps.label: Braise roulades

steps.text: Warm the red cabbage in a pot with the grated apple and the butter and let it simmer.
steps.tip: A grated apple and a little butter turn jarred red cabbage into almost grandma's version.
steps.label: Red cabbage

steps.text: Remove the roulades, strain the gravy, reduce a little and season. Serve with red cabbage and dumplings or potatoes.

title: Crispy Goose Legs
summary: Festive goose legs with red cabbage and dumplings. Much easier than a whole goose!

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 160 °C (fan). Pat the legs dry and rub them with salt, pepper, mugwort and marjoram.
steps.tip: Mugwort is the classic German goose herb. It makes the rich meat easier to digest.

steps.text: Cut the apples and onion into wedges, quarter the orange and put everything in a roasting dish. Place the legs on top, skin side up, and pour in 200 ml stock.
Roast in the oven, basting with the pan juices now and then.
steps.label: Legs in oven

steps.text: Turn the oven up to 220 °C with the grill on and let the legs crisp up. No more basting now!
steps.tip: For extra crispy skin: brush the skin with cold salted water first.
steps.label: Crisp skin

steps.text: Meanwhile, warm the red cabbage and cook the dumplings according to the package.
steps.label: Cabbage & dumplings

steps.text: Keep the legs warm. Strain the pan juices, skim off the fat and bring to a boil with the remaining stock.
Mix the cornstarch with a little water, thicken the gravy with it and season. Serve with red cabbage and dumplings.

title: Baked Apples with Vanilla Sauce
summary: Filled with marzipan, nuts and raisins. Smells like Advent.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (top/bottom heat). Wash the apples and generously cut out the cores.
steps.tip: Tart varieties like Boskoop or Elstar are ideal. They turn soft without falling apart.

steps.text: Pick the marzipan into small pieces and knead it with the nuts, raisins, cinnamon and 1 tbsp sugar.
Place the apples in a greased dish, fill them with the mixture and top each with a small knob of butter.
Bake until the apples are soft and the skin bursts.
steps.label: Bake apples

steps.text: For the vanilla sauce, stir the pudding powder smooth with 2 tbsp sugar and 5 tbsp milk.
Bring the remaining milk to a boil, stir in the mixed powder and let it bubble briefly while stirring.
steps.tip: With only half the pudding powder you get a pourable sauce instead of pudding. Brilliantly simple!
steps.label: Vanilla sauce

steps.text: Serve the baked apples with the warm vanilla sauce.

title: Cheese Fondue
summary: Creamy Swiss fondue for cozy evenings and New Year's Eve. A regular pot will do!

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water. Cut the baguette into bite-sized cubes, each with a bit of crust.
steps.tip: With crust, the bread stays on the fork and doesn't fall into the cheese.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Coarsely grate the cheese and toss it with the cornstarch.
Rub a pot with the halved garlic clove.
Heat the wine and a squeeze of lemon juice in the pot until it steams but doesn't boil.
steps.tip: The acidity of the wine and lemon keeps the cheese smooth and stops it from clumping.

steps.text: Add the cheese in batches and stir in a figure-eight until everything is melted and creamy.
steps.tip: Stirring in a figure-eight isn't superstition: it keeps everything moving evenly.
steps.label: Melt cheese

steps.text: Stir in the kirsch and season with pepper and nutmeg.
Put the pot on a burner or on the lowest heat at the table. Dip the bread and potatoes. Whoever loses their bread buys the next round!

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
summary: The real Roman way: guanciale, egg yolk, pecorino, pepper. No cream at all!

steps.text: Put on water for the pasta and salt it only lightly.
steps.tip: Use half the usual salt, the guanciale and pecorino are already very salty.

steps.text: Cut the guanciale into small strips. Finely grate the pecorino. Coarsely crush the pepper.
Stir 3 egg yolks and 1 whole egg with the pecorino and lots of pepper into a thick paste.
Put the guanciale in a cold pan, heat slowly and render the fat until crispy. Take the pan off the heat.
steps.tip: Start cold! The fat melts slowly and the pork crisps up evenly.
steps.label: Render guanciale

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti until al dente.
steps.label: Cook spaghetti

steps.text: Save a cup of pasta water. Add the spaghetti to the guanciale in the pan and toss. Keep the pan off the heat!
Thin the egg mixture with a splash of pasta water and pour it over the pasta while stirring constantly until you get a glossy, creamy sauce.
steps.tip: The residual heat is plenty. Too hot, and you get scrambled eggs instead of carbonara.

steps.text: Serve right away with extra pecorino and pepper.

title: Cacio e Pepe
summary: Just pasta, pecorino and pepper. Three ingredients, one trick, a whole lot of wow.

steps.text: Grate the pecorino as finely as possible. Coarsely crush the pepper.
steps.tip: Fine cheese melts faster and doesn't clump. Use the finest grater you have!

steps.text: Cook the pasta in a small amount of salted water, just enough to cover it.
steps.tip: Less water means more starch in the pasta water. That's what makes the sauce creamy.
steps.label: Cook pasta

steps.text: Toast the pepper in a large dry pan until fragrant. Add a ladle of pasta water and the butter.
steps.label: Toast pepper

steps.text: Stir the pecorino with a few tablespoons of lukewarm pasta water into a smooth paste.
Add the pasta to the pan and finish cooking it in the pepper water.
Take the pan off the heat, let it cool briefly and stir in the cheese paste. Thin with pasta water until the sauce is glossy.
steps.tip: Never add cheese to a hot pan! Too much heat turns pecorino into chewing gum.

steps.text: Serve right away with extra pepper.

title: Penne alla Vodka
summary: Creamy, slightly spicy tomato sauce. The vodka brings flavor, the alcohol cooks off.

steps.text: Put on salted water for the pasta. Finely chop the shallots and garlic.
Heat the olive oil and butter in a pan, sweat the shallots until soft and briefly fry the garlic and chili.
steps.label: Sweat shallots

steps.text: Add the tomato paste and toast while stirring until it turns dark red and sticks slightly to the bottom.
steps.tip: The most important step: toasted tomato paste gives the sauce its depth.
steps.label: Toast tomato paste

steps.text: Deglaze with the vodka and reduce almost completely.
steps.label: Reduce vodka

steps.text: Cook the penne until al dente.
steps.label: Cook penne

steps.text: Stir the cream into the sauce. Add the penne with a ladle of pasta water and toss until the sauce is glossy.
Fold in the Parmesan and serve with basil.

title: Spaghetti Puttanesca
summary: Punchy, salty, irresistible: tomatoes, olives, capers and anchovies. Almost all from the pantry.

steps.text: Put on water for the pasta and salt it.
Slice the garlic, halve the olives and chop the parsley.
Gently warm the olive oil with the garlic, anchovies and chili in a pan until the anchovies melt.
steps.tip: The anchovies dissolve completely. What's left is deep, savory flavor, not fishiness!
steps.label: Melt anchovies

steps.text: Add the tomatoes, olives and capers and let it reduce.
steps.label: Reduce sauce

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti until al dente.
steps.label: Cook spaghetti

steps.text: Add the pasta to the sauce with a little pasta water, toss and serve with parsley.

title: Viennese-Style Schnitzel with Cucumber Salad
summary: Paper-thin, with a wavy golden crust, plus a creamy cucumber salad.

steps.text: Thinly slice the cucumber, salt it and let it sit.
steps.label: Salt cucumber

steps.text: Pound the schnitzels between cling film with the bottom of a pan to about 4 mm thick. Season with salt and pepper.
steps.tip: Pounding thin is the secret to a tender schnitzel.

steps.text: Set up three deep plates: flour, beaten eggs, breadcrumbs. Coat the schnitzels in each one, pressing the crumbs on only lightly.
steps.tip: Don't press them on! Only a loose crust can puff up into waves later.

steps.text: Heat the clarified butter a finger deep in a large pan. Add the schnitzels and gently swirl the pan so the fat washes over the meat.
steps.tip: The swirling makes the crust puff up. That's how you get the famous waves.
steps.label: Schnitzel side 1

steps.text: Flip and fry the second side until golden. Then drain on paper towels.
steps.label: Schnitzel side 2

steps.text: Squeeze out the cucumber and mix with sour cream, vinegar, sugar, pepper and chopped dill.
Serve the schnitzels with lemon wedges and the cucumber salad.

title: Lemon Chicken with Crispy Potatoes
summary: Juicy chicken thighs and the crispiest roast potatoes, thanks to a pro trick.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C (fan). Pat the chicken thighs dry and salt them generously.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into large chunks. Finely chop 3 garlic cloves and the rosemary.
Bring the potatoes to a boil in a pot of water with 1 tbsp salt and the baking soda and simmer until soft on the outside.
steps.tip: The trick: the baking soda roughs up the surface. That gives you a glass-like crust!
steps.label: Par-boil potatoes

steps.text: Drain, let them steam dry briefly, return to the pot with the olive oil, rosemary and chopped garlic and shake hard until the edges are completely rough.
steps.tip: Shake hard. The rough starchy layer becomes a crunchy crust in the oven.

steps.text: Spread the potatoes on a tray. Add the chicken skin side up, and scatter one lemon cut into wedges and the rest of the garlic bulb, halved, in between.
Roast until the skin is crispy and the potatoes are golden. Turn the potatoes halfway through.
steps.label: Chicken in oven

steps.text: Drizzle with the juice of the second lemon and serve.

title: Paneer Butter Masala
summary: Seared paneer in a velvety tomato butter sauce. India's favorite curry, no meat needed.

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the amount of water and a little salt, then let it steam covered on low heat.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Cut the paneer into cubes and fry in the oil until golden all over. Remove.
steps.tip: Soak the fried paneer briefly in hot salted water. It turns wonderfully soft.
steps.label: Fry paneer

steps.text: Finely chop the onion, garlic and ginger and sweat them in the butter until soft. Add the spices and toast briefly.
steps.label: Sweat onions

steps.text: Add the tomatoes and sugar and simmer until the sauce is thick and the fat separates at the edges.
steps.tip: When the fat shows at the edges, the spices are properly cooked. That's the moment!
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Stir in the cream, add the paneer and let it warm through. Season with salt.
Sprinkle with cilantro and serve with rice and warm naan.

title: Palak Paneer
summary: Creamy spinach with ginger, garlic and seared paneer. Bright green and genuinely healthy.

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the amount of water and a little salt, then let it steam covered on low heat.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Wash the spinach and wilt it in boiling water. Plunge straight into ice-cold water, squeeze out and blend finely with the chili.
steps.tip: The ice water is the trick: it keeps the spinach bright green instead of olive brown.
steps.label: Blanch spinach

steps.text: Dice the paneer and fry in a little oil until golden. Remove.
steps.label: Fry paneer

steps.text: Heat the remaining oil and let the cumin seeds sizzle. Add the chopped onion, garlic and ginger and fry until golden.
steps.label: Fry onions

steps.text: Stir in the spinach purée and garam masala and simmer briefly. Add the cream and paneer and season with salt.
steps.tip: Only simmer briefly or the spinach loses its color.
steps.label: Simmer spinach

steps.text: Serve with the rice.

title: Chana Masala
summary: Spicy North Indian chickpea curry. Almost all from the pantry and ready in 30 minutes.

steps.text: Finely dice the onion, grate the garlic and ginger.
Heat the oil and fry the onion until deep golden brown.
steps.tip: Don't stop too early! Well-browned onions are the base of every good curry.
steps.label: Brown onion

steps.text: Add the garlic, ginger and all the spices and toast for a minute.
Add the tomatoes, rinsed chickpeas and 150 ml water and simmer.
steps.tip: Mash a few chickpeas with your spoon. It makes the sauce thick and creamy.
steps.label: Simmer curry

steps.text: Season with salt and lemon juice and sprinkle with cilantro.
Serve with naan and a dollop of yogurt.

title: Aloo Gobi
summary: Indian potato and cauliflower curry, dry-fried with turmeric and cumin.

steps.text: Cut the cauliflower into small florets and the potatoes into small cubes. Chop the onion, garlic and ginger and dice the tomatoes.
Heat the oil in a large pan and let the cumin seeds sizzle. Fry the onion, garlic and ginger until golden.
steps.label: Fry onions

steps.text: Add the potatoes, cauliflower, turmeric and 1 tsp salt and mix well. Cook covered over medium heat, turning now and then.
steps.tip: No water! The vegetables cook in their own steam and get lovely browned spots.
steps.label: Cook vegetables

steps.text: Add the tomatoes and garam masala and keep frying uncovered until everything is tender and lightly browned.
steps.label: Fry uncovered

steps.text: Season with lemon juice, sprinkle with cilantro and serve with naan.

title: Mushroom Mapo Tofu
summary: Silky tofu in a fiery Sichuan sauce. Mushrooms instead of mince, no compromise on flavor.

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the amount of water, then let it steam covered on low heat.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Cut the tofu into cubes and let it sit in gently simmering salted water.
steps.tip: The warm salted water firms up the silken tofu so it won't fall apart later.
steps.label: Poach tofu

steps.text: Chop the mushrooms very finely. Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan and crush them.
Heat the oil and fry the mushrooms until brown and crumbly. Add the garlic, ginger and bean paste and fry until the oil turns red.
steps.label: Fry mushrooms

steps.text: Add the stock and soy sauce, gently add the tofu and simmer.
steps.tip: Don't stir, just swirl the pan. That keeps the tofu in neat cubes.
steps.label: Simmer tofu

steps.text: Mix the cornstarch with 2 tbsp water and thicken the sauce. Sprinkle with Sichuan pepper and spring onions and serve with rice.

title: Crispy Tofu with Peanut Sauce
summary: Crispy outside, tender inside, with a creamy lime peanut sauce and broccoli.

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the amount of water, then let it steam covered on low heat.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Wrap the tofu in a kitchen towel and weigh it down with something heavy. Then tear it into chunks.
steps.tip: Torn instead of cut: the rough surface gets much crispier.
steps.label: Press tofu

steps.text: Toss the tofu with 1 tbsp soy sauce, then with the cornstarch. Fry in hot oil until crispy all over.
steps.label: Fry tofu

steps.text: Cut the broccoli into florets and cook in salted water until just tender.
steps.label: Cook broccoli

steps.text: Stir the peanut butter with the remaining soy sauce, syrup, grated garlic, lemon juice and a little warm water until smooth.
Plate the rice, broccoli and tofu, pour over the sauce and sprinkle with spring onions.

title: Tofu Pad Thai
summary: Rice noodles with tamarind, egg, tofu, peanuts and lime. Thailand's most famous street food.

steps.text: Soak the rice noodles in lukewarm water until pliable but still firm.
steps.tip: Don't boil them! Soaked noodles finish cooking in the pan and stay nicely chewy.
steps.label: Soak noodles

steps.text: Stir the tamarind, soy sauce, sugar and chili with 3 tbsp water. Dice the tofu, chop the garlic and roughly chop the peanuts.
Get the oil very hot in a wok and fry the tofu until golden. Briefly fry the garlic too.
steps.label: Fry tofu

steps.text: Add the drained noodles and the sauce and toss until the noodles have soaked it up.
steps.label: Toss noodles

steps.text: Push the noodles aside, crack the eggs into the middle, let them set briefly, then fold in.
steps.label: Set egg

steps.text: Fold in the bean sprouts and spring onions. Serve with peanuts and lime wedges.

title: Miso-Glazed Eggplant with Rice
summary: Japanese nasu dengaku: buttery soft eggplant with a caramelized miso glaze.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C (fan). Halve the eggplants lengthwise and score the flesh deeply in a diamond pattern.
steps.tip: The diamond pattern lets the heat and later the glaze sink deep into the flesh.

steps.text: Brush the cut sides with oil, salt lightly and roast cut side down until completely soft.
steps.label: Eggplant in oven

steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, bring to a boil with 200 ml water and let it steam covered. Drizzle with 1 tbsp rice vinegar.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Stir the miso, mirin and sugar together. Thinly slice the cucumber and toss with the remaining vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Turn the eggplants over, spread thickly with the miso paste and caramelize under the grill.
steps.tip: Stay close! The sugary glaze browns in seconds.
steps.label: Grill glaze

steps.text: Sprinkle with sesame and spring onions and serve with the rice and cucumber salad.

title: Bibimbap
summary: Korean rice bowl with colorful vegetables, a fried egg and spicy gochujang sauce.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and bring to a boil with 200 ml water, then let it steam covered.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Cut the carrots and zucchini into thin sticks and slice the mushrooms. Grate the garlic.
Fry each vegetable separately in a little oil and season with a splash of soy sauce. Just wilt the spinach and toss it with garlic and sesame oil.
steps.tip: Frying them one at a time pays off: every vegetable keeps its own flavor and color.
steps.label: Fry vegetables

steps.text: Stir the gochujang with 1 tbsp sesame oil, the sugar and 1 tbsp water into a sauce.
Fry the eggs until the whites are set and the yolks still runny.
steps.label: Fried eggs

steps.text: Put the rice in bowls, arrange the vegetables and kimchi in a circle on top and place the egg in the middle. Sprinkle with sesame and serve with the sauce. Mix everything well before eating!

title: Okonomiyaki
summary: Japanese cabbage pancake with tangy sauce and mayo. Savory, crispy and cheap.

steps.text: Cut the cabbage into very thin strips and the spring onions into rings.
Whisk the flour, eggs, 100 ml water and a pinch of salt until smooth. Fold in the cabbage and half the spring onions.
steps.tip: The batter should just hold the cabbage together. Lots of cabbage, little batter!

steps.text: Stir the ketchup, Worcestershire and soy sauce into a sauce.
Heat the oil in a pan, add half the batter about a finger thick and fry over medium heat.
steps.label: First side

steps.text: Flip it with the help of a plate and fry the second side. Repeat with the remaining batter.
steps.tip: To flip, put a plate on the pan, turn it over and slide the pancake back in.
steps.label: Second side

steps.text: Brush with the sauce, drizzle thin lines of mayo over the top and sprinkle with sesame and spring onions.

title: Cold Sesame Peanut Noodles
summary: Refreshing noodles with a creamy sesame peanut dressing, cucumber and herbs. Perfect for hot days.

steps.text: Cook the noodles according to the package, drain and rinse under cold water.
steps.tip: Rinse thoroughly in cold water: it stops the cooking and keeps the noodles from sticking.
steps.label: Cook noodles

steps.text: Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, sesame oil, vinegar, honey, grated garlic, lime juice and chili with 3 tbsp warm water until creamy.
Cut the cucumber and carrot into thin strips, the spring onions into rings and chop the peanuts.
Toss the noodles with the dressing and fold in the vegetables.
Sprinkle with peanuts and cilantro and serve cold.

title: Baked Falafel with Tahini
summary: Crispy oven-baked falafel with herbs, tahini sauce and pita. No deep-frying needed.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C (fan). Rinse the chickpeas and pat them very dry.
steps.tip: The drier the chickpeas, the crispier the falafel.

steps.text: Pulse the chickpeas, herbs, onion, 2 garlic cloves, the spices and 1 tsp salt in a food processor until coarse. Mix in the flour and baking powder.
steps.tip: Only pulse coarsely, don't purée to a paste. The texture makes good falafel.

steps.text: Shape small balls, flatten slightly, place on an oiled tray and brush with oil.
Bake in the oven, turning halfway.
steps.label: Bake falafel

steps.text: Stir the tahini with the yogurt, lemon juice, the remaining grated garlic clove, salt and a little water until creamy. Dice the tomatoes.
Warm the pita and fill with the falafel, tomatoes and tahini sauce.

title: Hummus Bowl with Crispy Chickpeas
summary: The creamiest hummus of your life with crispy chickpeas, cucumber and warm flatbread.

steps.text: Bring one can of chickpeas with their liquid and the baking soda to a boil and simmer until the skins loosen.
steps.tip: The Israeli secret: chickpeas cooked very soft with baking soda make super smooth hummus.
steps.label: Simmer chickpeas

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Rinse the second can, pat dry, toss with 2 tbsp oil, the paprika and salt and roast.
steps.label: Roast chickpeas

steps.text: Drain and rinse the cooked chickpeas. Blend for a long time with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, salt and 4 tbsp ice water.
steps.tip: Ice water and patience: blend for at least 3 minutes and it turns fluffy as a cloud.

steps.text: Dice the cucumber and tomatoes and mix with parsley, oil and salt.
Spread the hummus in bowls, top with the salad and crispy chickpeas, drizzle with olive oil and serve with warm flatbread.

title: Mujadara
summary: Lebanese lentils and rice with crispy fried onions and yogurt. Simple, cheap, brilliant.

steps.text: Par-cook the lentils in plenty of water until just firm, then drain.
steps.label: Cook lentils

steps.text: Cut the onions into thin half-rings and fry in the oil over medium heat until deep golden and crispy.
steps.tip: The onions are the star! Fry slowly until they're really dark and sweet.
steps.label: Crisp onions

steps.text: Remove half the onions. Add the rice, spices and lentils to the remaining onions and toast briefly.
Add 350 ml water and 1 tsp salt, bring to a boil, cook covered on low heat, then let it rest.
steps.label: Cook lentil rice

steps.text: Stir the yogurt with lemon juice and salt.
Serve the mujadara with the crispy onions, parsley and lemon yogurt.

title: Green Shakshuka
summary: Eggs in a bed of spinach, leek and herbs, with feta and warm bread.

steps.text: Slice the leek thinly and wash thoroughly. Chop the garlic.
Heat the oil in a pan and sweat the leek until soft. Briefly fry the garlic and cumin.
steps.label: Sweat leek

steps.text: Add the spinach in batches and let it wilt. Season with salt, pepper and a little lemon juice.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook until the whites are set.
steps.tip: Loosen the whites a little with a fork so they cook evenly while the yolk stays runny.
steps.label: Set eggs

steps.text: Sprinkle with crumbled feta, dill and chili and serve with warm bread.

title: Menemen
summary: Turkish scrambled eggs with peppers and tomatoes. Perfect for breakfast, lunch or dinner.

steps.text: Slice the peppers into rings and finely dice or grate the tomatoes.
Melt the butter in a pan and fry the peppers until soft.
steps.label: Fry peppers

steps.text: Add the tomatoes and Aleppo pepper and cook down until almost no liquid is left.
steps.tip: Reduce well, or the menemen turns watery.
steps.label: Reduce tomatoes

steps.text: Beat the eggs, salt them and add. Stir gently until just set and still creamy.
steps.label: Set eggs

steps.text: Sprinkle with feta, spring onions and parsley and eat straight from the pan with bread.

title: Çılbır (Turkish Eggs)
summary: Poached eggs on garlic yogurt with hot chili butter. Simple and spectacular.

steps.text: Stir the yogurt with grated garlic and salt and let it come to room temperature. Spread on plates.
steps.tip: Room-temperature yogurt matters, or it cools the eggs instantly.

steps.text: Bring a pot of water with the vinegar to a simmer. Crack each egg into a cup.
Stir the water to create a whirlpool and slide in the eggs one at a time. Poach until the whites are set.
steps.tip: Fresh eggs spread less. The whirlpool wraps the white around the yolk.
steps.label: Poach eggs

steps.text: Let the butter foam, take it off the heat and stir in the Aleppo pepper and paprika.
Place the eggs on the yogurt, drizzle with the chili butter, sprinkle with dill and serve with bread.

title: Spanakopita (Spinach Feta Pie)
summary: Greek classic: crispy filo pastry filled with spinach, feta and dill.

steps.text: Wash the spinach and wilt it in a large pot. Let it cool, squeeze out very well, then chop.
steps.tip: Squeeze it really well! Wet spinach makes the pastry soggy.
steps.label: Wilt spinach

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (fan). Mix the spinach with crumbled feta, eggs, chopped dill, spring onions, nutmeg and pepper.
Melt the butter. Line a dish with half the filo sheets, brushing each sheet with butter.
Spread the filling on top, cover with the remaining sheets, brushing each one. Score the top into portions.
steps.tip: Score before baking, or the crisp top shatters when you cut it later.

steps.text: Bake until golden brown.
steps.label: Bake spanakopita

steps.text: Let it cool briefly and serve warm or lukewarm.

title: Vegetable Tagine with Couscous
summary: Moroccan stew with chickpeas, sweet potato, apricots and ras el hanout.

steps.text: Chop the onion and garlic. Cut the sweet potato, carrots and zucchini into large chunks and halve the apricots.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot, sweat the onion until soft, then briefly toast the garlic and ras el hanout.
steps.label: Sweat onion

steps.text: Add the sweet potato, carrots, tomatoes, chickpeas, apricots and 300 ml stock. Braise covered.
steps.tip: The apricots melt away and add a subtle sweetness, typical of Morocco.
steps.label: Braise tagine

steps.text: Add the zucchini and keep braising until everything is tender.
steps.label: Braise zucchini

steps.text: Bring the remaining stock to a boil, pour over the couscous and let it swell covered. Fluff with a fork.
steps.label: Soak couscous

steps.text: Toast the almonds in a dry pan. Season the tagine with lemon juice and serve with couscous, yogurt, almonds and cilantro.

title: Maafe (West African Peanut Stew)
summary: Creamy stew with sweet potato, spinach and peanut butter. Warms you from the inside.

steps.text: Chop the onion, garlic and ginger. Peel and dice the sweet potatoes.
Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the onion until translucent. Briefly toast the garlic, ginger, tomato paste and spices.
steps.label: Sauté onion

steps.text: Add the sweet potatoes, tomatoes and stock, stir in the peanut butter and simmer.
steps.tip: Mix the peanut butter with a little hot stock first so it blends in without lumps.
steps.label: Simmer stew

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the water and some salt and let it steam covered.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Stir in the spinach and let it wilt. Season with lime juice and salt.
Serve with the rice and sprinkle with chopped peanuts.

title: Pasta e Ceci
summary: Roman pasta and chickpea soup with rosemary. Creamy, filling and almost all from the pantry.

steps.text: Slice the garlic and finely chop the rosemary needles.
Heat the oil in a pot and gently fry the garlic, rosemary and chili. Briefly toast the tomato paste.
steps.label: Fry garlic

steps.text: Add the rinsed chickpeas and stock and simmer. Then remove a third, blend and return it to the pot.
steps.tip: Blending part of it makes the soup creamy without any cream.
steps.label: Simmer chickpeas

steps.text: Cook the pasta right in the soup, stirring often. Add water if needed.
steps.label: Cook pasta

steps.text: Season with salt and pepper and serve with Parmesan and a good drizzle of olive oil.

title: Pasta al Limone
summary: Spaghetti in a silky lemon butter Parmesan sauce. Ten minutes, five ingredients, pure joy.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Finely zest the lemons, squeeze the juice and finely grate the Parmesan.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente.
steps.label: Cook spaghetti

steps.text: Melt the butter with the lemon zest in a large pan. Add a ladle of pasta water and bring to a boil.
Add the spaghetti to the pan, take it off the heat and toss in the Parmesan and lemon juice until a creamy sauce forms.
steps.tip: Taking it off the heat matters: otherwise the cheese clumps and the lemon turns bitter.

steps.text: Serve with pepper and basil.

title: Pasta with Pesto Genovese
summary: Just like in Liguria: pesto with potatoes and green beans cooked right in the pasta water.

steps.text: Pound or briefly blend the basil leaves, garlic, pine nuts and a pinch of salt. Stir in the cheese and olive oil.
steps.tip: Pulse briefly instead of blending long. Heat from the blender turns basil dark and bitter.

steps.text: Peel and finely dice the potatoes and cut the beans into pieces. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Add the potatoes to the water, then the pasta and beans, and cook everything together.
steps.label: Cook pasta & veg

steps.text: Save a cup of pasta water, drain everything and toss with the pesto and a little pasta water.
steps.tip: The potato starch makes the pesto wonderfully creamy. That's how they do it in Genoa!

steps.text: Serve right away.

title: Spaghetti with Tomato Butter Sauce
summary: Just tomatoes, butter and an onion. Three ingredients, slowly simmered, wonderfully mellow.

steps.text: Peel and halve the onion. Put it in a pot with the tomatoes, butter and a pinch of salt.
Simmer slowly, crushing the tomatoes with a wooden spoon now and then.
steps.tip: No garlic, no herbs. The butter rounds off the acidity and makes the sauce velvety.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti in salted water until al dente.
steps.label: Cook spaghetti

steps.text: Remove the onion from the sauce (or secretly snack on it) and season with salt.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and serve with Parmesan.

title: Ricotta Gnocchi with Sage Butter
summary: Feather-light gnocchi made from ricotta instead of potatoes, ready in 30 minutes.

steps.text: Let the ricotta drain in a sieve.
steps.tip: The drier the ricotta, the less flour you need and the fluffier the gnocchi.
steps.label: Drain ricotta

steps.text: Mix the ricotta, egg, half the Parmesan, nutmeg, salt and pepper. Knead in the flour only briefly.
Roll the dough into finger-thick ropes and cut into 2 cm pieces.
Cook in simmering salted water until they float, then let them sit one more minute.
steps.label: Cook gnocchi

steps.text: Brown the butter with the sage and toss the gnocchi in it.
steps.label: Sage butter

steps.text: Serve with the remaining Parmesan and a little lemon zest.

title: Lemon Risotto with Peas
summary: Fresh and creamy with lemon, peas, mint and Parmesan. Tastes like spring.

steps.text: Keep the stock hot in a pot. Finely dice the shallots.
Heat the oil in a wide pot, sweat the shallots, add the rice and toast until translucent.
steps.label: Toast rice

steps.text: Deglaze with the wine. Then add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring until absorbed.
steps.tip: The stock must be hot. Cold stock stops the cooking and makes the rice uneven.
steps.label: Stir risotto

steps.text: Add the peas and cook until the rice is creamy and al dente.
steps.label: Cook peas

steps.text: Take off the heat and vigorously stir in the butter, Parmesan, lemon zest and some juice. Let it rest covered.
steps.tip: Vigorous stirring with cold butter is called 'mantecatura'. It's what makes risotto truly creamy.
steps.label: Let rest

steps.text: Serve with chopped mint and pepper.

title: Eggplant Parmigiana
summary: Layers of fried eggplant, tomato sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan. Southern Italy's summer treasure.

steps.text: Slice the eggplants lengthwise 1 cm thick, salt them and let them sit. Then pat dry.
steps.label: Salt eggplant

steps.text: For the sauce, fry the garlic in 2 tbsp oil, add the tomatoes, salt and simmer until thick. Add basil.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Fry the eggplant slices in batches in the remaining oil until golden. Preheat the oven to 190 °C.
steps.tip: Instead of frying, you can brush them with oil and roast them. Lighter and just as tasty.
steps.label: Fry eggplant

steps.text: Layer sauce, eggplant, mozzarella and Parmesan in a dish. Finish with sauce and Parmesan.
Bake until bubbling and golden.
steps.label: Bake parmigiana

steps.text: Let it rest at least 10 minutes, then cut.
steps.tip: Resting matters or it all slides apart. It actually tastes best lukewarm.

title: Pizza Margherita
summary: Crispy pizza from your home oven. With the hot tray trick it's almost like a pizzeria.

steps.text: Knead the flour, yeast, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp oil and 190 ml lukewarm water into a smooth, soft dough. Cover and let it rise.
steps.tip: Even better: let the dough rise overnight in the fridge. It adds flavor and bubbles in the crust.
steps.label: Let dough rise

steps.text: Preheat the oven to its highest setting (at least 250 °C) with an upside-down baking tray inside.
steps.tip: The hot tray stands in for a pizza stone. That's what makes the base crispy.
steps.label: Preheat oven

steps.text: Crush the tomatoes with your hands and season with salt, oregano and grated garlic. Tear the mozzarella and let it drain.
Halve the dough, press it thin with your fingers (leave the edge thicker) and place on baking paper. Top with sauce and mozzarella.
Slide the pizza on its paper onto the hot tray and bake until the crust is golden.
steps.label: Bake pizza

steps.text: Serve with basil and a drizzle of olive oil. Bake the second pizza the same way.

title: Stovetop Mac and Cheese
summary: Extremely creamy, one pot, 15 minutes. The trick comes from a can of evaporated milk.
