steps.text: Cook the macaroni in a pot with just enough salted water to cover, until almost all the water is absorbed.
steps.tip: Little water, no draining: the starch stays in the pot and helps the sauce.
steps.label: Cook macaroni

steps.text: Grate the cheese and toss with the cornstarch. Whisk the egg with 150 ml evaporated milk and the mustard.
Turn the heat to low, add the egg mixture and cheese and stir until the sauce is smooth and creamy.
steps.tip: Evaporated milk keeps the cheese smooth. The sauce never turns grainy or greasy.

steps.text: Loosen with a little more evaporated milk, season with salt and plenty of pepper and serve right away.

title: Spaghetti alla Nerano
summary: From the Amalfi Coast: fried zucchini melts with cheese into an unbelievably creamy sauce.

steps.text: Slice the zucchini thinly.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the zucchini in batches until golden. Drain and salt.
steps.tip: Fry them truly golden! The browned flavor is the secret of this dish.
steps.label: Fry zucchini

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti in salted water 2 minutes less than the package says.
steps.label: Cook spaghetti

steps.text: Mash two thirds of the zucchini with the garlic and a little pasta water in a pan. Add the pasta and finish cooking with pasta water.
steps.label: Finish cooking

steps.text: Take off the heat and stir in the butter, cheese and basil until the sauce turns creamy.
steps.tip: Off the heat the cheese melts silky instead of turning stringy.

steps.text: Serve with the remaining zucchini and pepper.

title: Spinach Ricotta Lasagna
summary: Juicy vegetable lasagna with spinach, ricotta, tomato sauce and golden mozzarella.

steps.text: Chop the onion and garlic and sweat them in the oil. Add the tomatoes, salt and simmer. Add basil.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Wilt the spinach, squeeze it well, chop and mix with the ricotta, egg, half the Parmesan, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
steps.label: Wilt spinach

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 190 °C. Layer sauce, sheets and spinach-ricotta in a dish. Finish with sauce.
steps.tip: The sauce can be a bit runny. The sheets soak up a lot while baking.

steps.text: Top with mozzarella and the remaining Parmesan and bake.
steps.label: Bake lasagna

steps.text: Let it rest briefly, then cut.
steps.label: Let rest

title: Gnocchi alla Sorrentina
summary: Gnocchi baked in tomato sauce with melting mozzarella. Comfort food from Sorrento.

steps.text: Preheat the oven grill to 220 °C. Fry the garlic in the oil, add the tomatoes, salt and simmer.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Cook the gnocchi in salted water until they float.
steps.label: Cook gnocchi

steps.text: Mix the gnocchi and basil into the sauce and transfer to a dish. Top with torn mozzarella and Parmesan.
Grill until the cheese bubbles.
steps.tip: Drain the mozzarella well first or it turns watery.
steps.label: Grill cheese

steps.text: Serve with fresh basil.

title: Minestrone
summary: Italian vegetable soup with beans, pasta and the secret tip: Parmesan rind.

steps.text: Finely dice the onion, carrots, celery and zucchini, chop the garlic and cut the cabbage into strips.
Heat the oil in a large pot and slowly sweat the onion, carrots and celery until soft.
steps.label: Sweat vegetables

steps.text: Add the garlic, zucchini, tomatoes, stock and the Parmesan rind and simmer.
steps.tip: Never throw away Parmesan rind! In soup it adds savoriness and depth.
steps.label: Simmer soup

steps.text: Add the beans, cabbage and pasta and keep simmering until the pasta is cooked.
steps.label: Cook pasta

steps.text: Remove the rind, season and serve with grated Parmesan and olive oil.

title: Ribollita
summary: Tuscan bread and bean stew with black kale. Even better the next day.

steps.text: Dice the onion, carrots and celery, chop the garlic, strip the kale from its stems and chop roughly.
Heat the oil in a large pot and slowly sweat the vegetables with rosemary until soft.
steps.label: Sweat vegetables

steps.text: Add the garlic, tomatoes, kale, beans and stock and simmer.
steps.label: Simmer stew

steps.text: Tear the bread into pieces and stir it in until it falls apart and thickens the stew.
steps.tip: Ribollita means 'reboiled'. It's best reheated the next day.
steps.label: Cook in bread

steps.text: Serve with lots of olive oil, pepper and Parmesan.

title: Tomato Galette
summary: Rustic tart with sun-ripened tomatoes, ricotta and thyme in shortcrust pastry.

steps.text: Slice the tomatoes, salt them and let them drain on paper towels.
steps.tip: Draining matters, or the base goes soggy.
steps.label: Drain tomatoes

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Stir the ricotta with the Parmesan, grated garlic, thyme and pepper.
Unroll the pastry on a tray, spread the ricotta in the middle leaving a 4 cm border. Arrange the tomatoes on top.
Fold the border over the filling, brush with beaten egg and drizzle the tomatoes with oil.
Bake until golden brown.
steps.label: Bake galette

steps.text: Let it cool a little and serve with fresh thyme.

title: Pasta with Green Asparagus
summary: Seared green asparagus, lemon, Parmesan and toasted breadcrumbs. Spring on a plate.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Snap off the woody ends of the asparagus and cut the spears diagonally into pieces.
steps.tip: Just bend it: the asparagus snaps exactly where it turns woody.

steps.text: Toast the breadcrumbs in 1 tbsp oil until golden and mix with some lemon zest.
steps.label: Toast crumbs

steps.text: Cook the pasta until al dente.
steps.label: Cook pasta

steps.text: Sear the asparagus in the remaining oil over high heat until browned. Briefly fry the garlic and chili.
steps.label: Sear asparagus

steps.text: Add the pasta to the pan with some pasta water, butter, Parmesan and lemon juice and toss until glossy.
Serve topped with the breadcrumbs and pepper.

title: Pea and Mint Soup
summary: Bright green, velvety soup in 20 minutes. With crumbled feta and croutons.

steps.text: Dice the onion and sweat it in the butter.
steps.label: Sweat onion

steps.text: Add the stock and bring to a boil, then add the frozen peas and simmer briefly.
steps.tip: Only simmer briefly! That keeps the peas' color and sweetness.
steps.label: Simmer peas

steps.text: Dice the bread and toast in a pan until golden.
steps.label: Toast croutons

steps.text: Add the mint leaves and cream to the soup and blend finely. Season with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Serve with croutons and crumbled feta.

title: Spanish Tortilla
summary: Spanish potato omelette, juicy inside, golden outside. Delicious warm or cold.

steps.text: Peel the potatoes and slice thinly. Cut the onion into thin strips.
Heat the oil in a pan and gently cook the potatoes and onion over medium heat until soft, without browning.
steps.tip: The potatoes cook in the oil like a confit. Save the oil afterward, it's full of flavor!
steps.label: Confit potatoes

steps.text: Beat the eggs with 1 tsp salt. Drain the potatoes, mix them into the eggs and let it sit.
steps.label: Let it soak

steps.text: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a smaller pan, pour in the mixture and cook over medium heat until set.
steps.label: First side

steps.text: Flip with a plate and cook the second side until just set inside but still juicy.
steps.tip: Flip with confidence! Plate on the pan, turn it over in one go and slide it back in.
steps.label: Second side

steps.text: Let it rest briefly and cut into wedges.

title: Vegetable Paella
summary: Saffron rice with peppers, green beans and artichokes. With a crispy crust at the bottom.

steps.text: Dice the onion, pepper and garlic, halve the beans and grate the tomatoes. Soak the saffron in a little warm stock.
Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the onion, pepper and beans. Add the garlic, paprika and tomatoes and cook down.
steps.label: Fry vegetables

steps.text: Scatter in the rice, stir briefly, then pour in the hot stock with saffron and 1 tsp salt. Arrange the artichokes on top.
Simmer over medium heat without stirring until the rice has absorbed the liquid.
steps.tip: No more stirring from here! That's how you get the coveted socarrat, the crispy crust.
steps.label: Simmer paella

steps.text: Turn up the heat briefly until it crackles, then take off the heat and let it rest covered with a towel.
steps.label: Let rest

steps.text: Serve with parsley and lemon wedges.

title: Tomato Soup with Grilled Cheese
summary: Velvety roasted tomato soup and crispy cheese toasties for dipping. The ultimate comfort food.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Drain the tomatoes (keep the juice) and roast them on a tray with onion wedges, garlic and oil.
steps.tip: Roasting brings sweetness and depth. Canned tomatoes then taste garden-fresh.
steps.label: Roast tomatoes

steps.text: Put everything in a pot with the tomato juice, stock and sugar, bring to a boil and blend finely. Stir in the cream and basil and season.
Butter the outside of the bread slices and fill pairs with grated cheddar.
Fry in a pan over medium heat on both sides until golden and the cheese melts.
steps.tip: Medium heat is the trick: golden outside, melted inside, nothing burnt.
steps.label: Fry toasties

steps.text: Halve the toasties and serve with the soup for dipping.

title: Spinach Dumplings with Brown Butter
summary: South Tyrolean classic made from bread, spinach and mountain cheese, with nutty butter and Parmesan.

ingredients.name: Dumpling bread or stale bread rolls

steps.text: Wilt the spinach briefly in boiling water, rinse in cold water, squeeze very well and chop finely.
steps.label: Blanch spinach

steps.text: Finely dice the onion and garlic and sweat in 1 tbsp butter.
steps.label: Sweat onion

steps.text: Pour the lukewarm milk over the bread. Add the spinach, onions, eggs, diced mountain cheese, flour, nutmeg, salt and pepper and mix well. Let it rest.
steps.tip: The resting time matters: the bread soaks everything up, so the dumplings hold together while cooking.
steps.label: Rest dough

steps.text: Shape 8 dumplings with wet hands and let them simmer gently in salted water until cooked.
steps.tip: Cook one test dumpling first. If it falls apart, add a little more flour or breadcrumbs.
steps.label: Cook dumplings

steps.text: Brown the remaining butter in a pan until nutty.
steps.label: Brown butter

steps.text: Drizzle the dumplings with brown butter and sprinkle with Parmesan.

title: Bread Dumplings with Creamy Mushrooms
summary: Bavarian bread dumplings with creamy mushroom sauce. Autumn soul food at its best.

steps.text: Cut the rolls into small cubes, pour over the warm milk and let soak.
steps.label: Soak bread

steps.text: Finely dice one onion, sweat it with half the parsley in 1 tbsp butter and knead into the bread with the eggs, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
steps.tip: Don't knead too hard, just until combined. That keeps the dumplings light.

steps.text: Shape 6 dumplings with wet hands and let them simmer in salted water without boiling.
steps.label: Cook dumplings

steps.text: Slice the mushrooms and sear them in batches in the remaining butter over high heat.
steps.tip: Fry in batches: too many mushrooms at once steam in their own water instead of browning.
steps.label: Sear mushrooms

steps.text: Dice the second onion and fry it too. Deglaze with the wine, add the stock and cream and simmer until creamy.
steps.label: Reduce sauce

steps.text: Season, add the remaining parsley and serve with the dumplings.

title: Kaiserschmarrn
summary: Fluffy torn-up pancake with raisins, powdered sugar and applesauce. Austria's favorite dessert as a main.

steps.text: Separate the eggs. Whisk the yolks with the milk, flour, vanilla sugar and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Beat the egg whites with the sugar until stiff and gently fold into the batter.
steps.tip: The beaten whites make the schmarrn so fluffy. Fold, don't stir!

steps.text: Melt half the butter in a large pan, pour in the batter, scatter over the raisins and let it set over medium heat.
steps.label: Set batter

steps.text: Quarter it, flip and tear into pieces with two forks. Add the remaining butter and fry until golden.
steps.label: Fry schmarrn

steps.text: Dust with 1 tbsp powdered sugar and let it caramelize briefly.
steps.tip: The caramelized powdered sugar gives the typical crispy edges.

steps.text: Dust with the remaining powdered sugar and serve with applesauce.

title: Rice Pudding with Hot Cherries
summary: Creamy rice pudding like grandma's, with cinnamon sugar and warm sour cherries.

steps.text: Bring the milk to a boil with the butter, 2 tbsp sugar, vanilla sugar and a pinch of salt. Stir in the rice.
Let it swell covered on the lowest heat, stirring now and then.
steps.tip: Lowest heat and frequent stirring, or it burns on the bottom.
steps.label: Simmer rice pudding

steps.text: Bring the cherries and their juice to a boil. Mix the cornstarch with a little juice and thicken the cherries.
steps.label: Thicken cherries

steps.text: Mix the cinnamon with the remaining sugar.
Serve the rice pudding with cinnamon sugar and hot cherries.

title: Roasted Beets with Goat Cheese
summary: Roasted beets with creamy goat cheese, walnuts, honey and lamb's lettuce.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Peel the beets and cut into wedges.
steps.tip: Wear gloves! Beets stain your fingers for days.

steps.text: Toss with 2 tbsp oil, thyme, salt and pepper and roast until soft and caramelized at the edges.
steps.label: Roast beets

steps.text: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan and glaze with 1 tbsp honey.
steps.label: Toast walnuts

steps.text: Whisk the balsamic, remaining honey, remaining oil, salt and pepper into a dressing.
Arrange the lamb's lettuce and beets, crumble over the goat cheese, top with walnuts and dressing. Serve with baguette.

title: Lentil Salad with Roasted Vegetables
summary: Savory beluga lentils with roasted vegetables, feta and mustard vinaigrette. Great warm or cold.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C. Cut the pepper, zucchini and onion into pieces, toss with 2 tbsp oil and salt and roast.
steps.label: Roast vegetables

steps.text: Cook the lentils in unsalted water until just tender and drain.
steps.tip: Salt only after cooking so the lentils stay tender and don't burst.
steps.label: Cook lentils

steps.text: Whisk the vinegar, mustard, honey, remaining oil, salt and pepper and marinate the warm lentils in it.
steps.tip: Warm lentils soak up the dressing far better than cold ones.

steps.text: Fold in the roasted vegetables, parsley and arugula and crumble over the feta.

title: Black Bean Tacos
summary: Spiced black beans, avocado, pickled onions and lime in warm tortillas.

steps.text: Slice the red onion into thin rings and pickle with the juice of one lime, the sugar and a pinch of salt.
steps.tip: Quick-pickled onions turn pink and mild. They make every taco better!
steps.label: Pickle onions

steps.text: Chop the garlic and fry briefly in the oil with the spices. Add the beans with a little of their liquid, simmer and roughly mash.
steps.label: Simmer beans

steps.text: Mash the avocado with lime juice and salt. Dice the tomatoes.
Warm the tortillas briefly on both sides in a dry pan.
Fill the tortillas with beans, avocado, tomatoes, onions, cheese, sour cream and cilantro.

title: Corn and Pepper Quesadillas
summary: Crispy tortillas filled with melted cheese, corn, peppers and jalapeños.

steps.text: Finely dice the pepper and fry it with the drained corn in a little oil.
steps.label: Fry vegetables

steps.text: Grate the cheese. Chop the spring onions and jalapeños.
Cover half of each tortilla with cheese, vegetables, spring onions and jalapeños and fold over.
steps.tip: Put cheese on the bottom and top: it acts like glue and holds everything together.

steps.text: Fry in a pan with a little oil over medium heat until crispy on both sides.
steps.label: Fry quesadillas

steps.text: Cut into wedges and serve with sour cream, salsa, cilantro and lime.

title: Huevos Rancheros
summary: Mexican breakfast: fried eggs on tortillas with spicy tomato salsa, beans and avocado.

steps.text: Chop the onion, garlic and chili and fry in 1 tbsp oil. Add the tomatoes and cumin, salt and simmer.
steps.label: Simmer salsa

steps.text: Rinse the beans and warm them in a small pot.
steps.label: Warm beans

steps.text: Fry the tortillas briefly in a little oil until slightly crispy.
steps.tip: A quick fry makes the tortillas sturdy so they don't go soggy under the salsa.

steps.text: Fry the eggs.
steps.label: Fried eggs

steps.text: Top the tortillas with beans, egg and salsa. Serve with avocado, feta and cilantro.

title: Spring Frittata
summary: Italian oven omelette with green asparagus, peas, goat cheese and herbs.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Cut the asparagus into pieces and the spring onions into rings.
Heat the oil in an ovenproof pan and fry the asparagus and spring onions. Add the peas.
steps.label: Fry vegetables

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the cream, Parmesan, chives, salt and pepper and pour over the vegetables. Dot with the goat cheese.
Let it set briefly on the stove until the edge firms up, then finish in the oven.
steps.tip: Take it out while the center still wobbles slightly. It keeps cooking and stays juicy.
steps.label: Bake frittata

steps.text: Let it rest briefly, cut into wedges and serve.

title: Gratin Dauphinois
summary: French potato gratin cooked in cream and garlic. Meltingly soft with a golden crust.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Peel the potatoes and slice them very thinly.
Bring the cream, milk, crushed garlic, thyme, nutmeg, salt and pepper to a boil. Simmer the potatoes in it.
steps.tip: The pro trick: pre-cook the potatoes in the cream. The starch binds the sauce and nothing curdles.
steps.label: Simmer potatoes

steps.text: Butter a dish, pour in the potatoes and cream (remove the garlic and thyme) and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake until the top is golden and a knife slides in easily.
steps.label: Bake gratin

steps.text: Dress the lamb's lettuce with oil, balsamic and salt and serve with the gratin.

title: Baked Potatoes with Herb Quark
summary: Crispy baked potatoes with creamy herb quark and radishes. Simple and so good.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Wash and dry the potatoes, prick all over with a fork and rub with oil and coarse salt.
steps.tip: Oil and coarse salt make the skin as crispy as chips.

steps.text: Bake the potatoes directly on the rack until completely soft inside.
steps.label: Bake potatoes

steps.text: Stir the quark with the schmand, chopped herbs, grated garlic, linseed oil, salt and pepper.
steps.tip: A splash of linseed oil is the Spreewald classic: nutty and very traditional.

steps.text: Slice the radishes thinly.
Cut a cross into the potatoes, squeeze them open, add a knob of butter and serve with the herb quark and radishes.

title: Kohlrabi Schnitzel with Potato Salad
summary: Breaded kohlrabi slices, crispy outside and tender inside, with a light potato salad.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Peel the kohlrabi, cut into 1 cm slices and pre-cook in salted water.
steps.tip: Pre-cook briefly so the kohlrabi is tender inside when the crust turns golden.
steps.label: Pre-cook kohlrabi

steps.text: Peel and slice the potatoes and toss with hot stock, vinegar, mustard, 3 tbsp oil, salt, pepper and chives.
Pat the kohlrabi dry, salt it and coat in flour, beaten eggs and breadcrumbs.
Heat the remaining oil and fry the schnitzels on both sides until golden.
steps.label: Fry schnitzel

steps.text: Serve with lemon wedges and the potato salad.

title: Lentils with Spätzle
summary: Swabia's national dish: tangy lentils with spätzle. Here in a vegetarian version.

steps.text: Finely dice the onion and soup vegetables and sweat them in the butter. Briefly toast the tomato paste and flour.
steps.label: Sweat vegetables

steps.text: Add the lentils, stock and bay leaf and simmer until the lentils are soft.
steps.label: Simmer lentils

steps.text: Season boldly sweet and sour with vinegar, mustard, sugar, salt and pepper.
steps.tip: The vinegar is the key! A little more is better, that's how it tastes in Swabia.

steps.text: Fry the spätzle in a pan with a little butter until golden.
steps.label: Fry spätzle

steps.text: Serve the lentils with the spätzle and parsley.

title: Creamed Savoy Cabbage with Fried Egg
summary: Tender savoy cabbage in nutmeg cream with boiled potatoes and a fried egg. Simple and wonderful.

steps.text: Peel the potatoes and boil in salted water.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Quarter the cabbage, remove the core and cut into thin strips. Dice the onion.
Sweat the onion in half the butter, add the cabbage and sweat briefly.
steps.label: Sweat cabbage

steps.text: Add the stock and cream and simmer until the cabbage is soft and creamy. Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
steps.tip: Nutmeg and savoy cabbage are a dream team. Freshly grated tastes best.
steps.label: Reduce cream

steps.text: Fry the eggs in the remaining butter.
steps.label: Fried eggs

steps.text: Serve the cabbage with the potatoes and fried egg.

title: Pumpkin Chickpea Curry
summary: Creamy yellow curry with Hokkaido squash, chickpeas, spinach and coconut milk.

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the water and some salt and let it steam covered.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Deseed the squash and dice it, skin on. Chop the onion, garlic and ginger.
Heat the oil, fry the onion, garlic and ginger and briefly toast the spices.
steps.label: Fry onion

steps.text: Add the squash, coconut milk, rinsed chickpeas and 100 ml water and simmer until the squash is soft.
steps.tip: Mash a few squash cubes to make the sauce nice and thick.
steps.label: Simmer curry

steps.text: Stir in the spinach, season with soy sauce and lime juice and serve with the rice.

title: Mushroom Stroganoff
summary: Seared mushrooms in a tangy paprika sour cream sauce with ribbon noodles. Hearty without meat.

steps.text: Quarter the mushrooms, cut the onion into strips, chop the garlic and cut the gherkins into sticks.
Heat the oil until very hot and sear the mushrooms in batches until brown.
steps.tip: Only salt once they're browned. Salt draws out water and stops them browning.
steps.label: Sear mushrooms

steps.text: Cook the noodles in salted water until al dente.
steps.label: Cook noodles

steps.text: Add the butter, onion and garlic to the mushrooms and fry until soft. Briefly toast the paprika, then deglaze with the stock and soy sauce.
steps.label: Fry onions

steps.text: Take off the heat, stir in the schmand, mustard and gherkins and season.
steps.tip: Don't boil the schmand, or it will split.

steps.text: Serve with the noodles and parsley.

title: Potato Noodles with Sauerkraut
summary: Golden fried potato noodles with wine sauerkraut, onions and apple. Christmas market feeling at home.

steps.text: Cut the onion into strips and grate the apple.
Sweat half the onions in a little butter, add the sauerkraut, apple, caraway, bay leaf, sugar and 100 ml water and simmer.
steps.tip: The grated apple takes the edge off the kraut and makes it mild and fruity.
steps.label: Simmer sauerkraut

steps.text: Fry the potato noodles in the oil and remaining butter with the rest of the onions until golden all over.
steps.label: Fry noodles

steps.text: Fold in the sauerkraut, season with salt and pepper and serve with parsley.

title: Halloumi Burger
summary: Grilled halloumi with roasted pepper, arugula and garlic yogurt in a brioche bun.

steps.text: Cut the pepper into wide strips and the onion into rings and fry in a grill pan with 1 tbsp oil until soft.
steps.label: Fry peppers

steps.text: Stir the yogurt with grated garlic, lemon juice and salt.
Cut the halloumi into thick slices and grill without oil on both sides until golden. Drizzle with honey and chili.
steps.tip: Halloumi needs no oil. Only flip once it releases from the pan by itself.
steps.label: Grill halloumi

steps.text: Split the buns and toast the cut sides briefly.
Fill the buns with yogurt, arugula, peppers, onions and halloumi.

title: Leek and Cheese Quiche
summary: Buttery shortcrust with a creamy leek and Gruyère filling. A dream served lukewarm with salad.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Line a tart tin with the pastry, prick with a fork and blind-bake.
steps.tip: Blind-baking prevents a soggy bottom. Weigh down baking paper with dried beans.
steps.label: Blind-bake base

steps.text: Slice the leek into rings, wash thoroughly and sweat in the butter until soft. Season with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Sweat leek

steps.text: Whisk the eggs with the cream, grated cheese, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Spread the leek over the base and pour over the egg mixture. Turn the oven down to 180 °C and bake until the filling is set.
steps.label: Bake quiche

steps.text: Let it cool a little. Dress the lamb's lettuce with oil, balsamic and salt and serve with the quiche.

title: Butter Chicken
summary: Tender yogurt-marinated chicken in a velvety tomato butter sauce. The curry classic from Delhi.

steps.text: Cut the chicken into pieces and marinate with the yogurt, half the spices, 1 grated garlic clove and salt.
steps.tip: Yogurt makes the meat butter-tender. Overnight in the fridge is even better.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the water and some salt and let it steam covered.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Cook the chicken under the oven grill or in a very hot pan until charred in spots.
steps.label: Char chicken

steps.text: Finely chop the onion, remaining garlic and ginger and sweat them in the butter. Briefly toast the remaining spices.
steps.label: Sweat onions

steps.text: Add the tomatoes and sugar and simmer. Blend smooth, add the cream and chicken and let it simmer gently.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Serve with cilantro, rice and naan.

title: Pad Krapow (Thai Basil Chicken)
summary: Thailand's favorite stir-fry: minced chicken, chili, basil and a fried egg over rice.

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the water and let it steam covered.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Pound the garlic and chili coarsely in a mortar or chop finely. Cut the beans into short pieces. Stir the sauces and sugar together.
steps.tip: Pounding instead of chopping releases much more flavor.

steps.text: Fry the eggs in 3 tbsp hot oil until crispy, basting with the oil.
steps.tip: Thai style: the white should bubble up and get crispy edges.
steps.label: Fried eggs

steps.text: Get the wok very hot, briefly fry the garlic and chili, then add the mince and fry until crumbly.
steps.label: Fry mince

steps.text: Add the beans and sauce and fry briefly. Take off the heat and fold in the basil leaves.
steps.label: Fry beans

steps.text: Serve over rice with the fried egg.

title: Teriyaki Salmon with Rice
summary: Glossy glazed salmon with homemade teriyaki sauce, rice and bok choy.

steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, bring to a boil with 200 ml water and let it steam covered.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Stir the soy sauce, mirin, honey, grated ginger and garlic together.
Pat the salmon dry and fry skin side down in hot oil until crispy.
steps.tip: Don't move it! The skin releases by itself once it's crispy.
steps.label: Salmon skin side

steps.text: Flip, pour in the sauce and reduce until syrupy, basting the salmon again and again.
steps.label: Glaze

steps.text: Halve the bok choy and steam briefly in a second pan with a little water, covered.
steps.label: Steam bok choy

steps.text: Serve with rice and sprinkle with sesame and spring onions.

title: German Chicken Fricassee
summary: Grandma's chicken fricassee with asparagus, mushrooms and peas in a creamy white sauce. With rice.

steps.text: Bring the stock to a boil and gently poach the chicken in it on low heat. Remove and keep the stock.
steps.tip: Poaching instead of frying keeps the chicken juicy, and the stock becomes the sauce.
steps.label: Poach chicken

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the water and some salt and let it steam covered.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Slice the mushrooms, dice the onion and sweat both in the butter. Dust with the flour and cook briefly.
steps.label: Sweat mushrooms

steps.text: Gradually whisk in 400 ml stock and simmer until the sauce thickens. Add the cream.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Pull the chicken into pieces and warm through in the sauce with the asparagus and peas. Season with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
steps.label: Warm through

steps.text: Serve with rice and parsley.

title: Chicken Paprikash
summary: Hungarian classic: chicken in creamy paprika sauce with sour cream and dumplings.

steps.text: Salt the chicken and brown it all over in the oil. Remove.
steps.label: Brown chicken

steps.text: Finely dice the onions and sweat in the pan fat until soft and golden. Briefly fry the garlic.
steps.label: Sweat onions

steps.text: Take the pot off the heat, stir in the paprika, then add the peppers, tomato, stock and chicken. Braise covered.
steps.tip: Always stir in paprika off the heat, or it turns bitter.
steps.label: Braise chicken

steps.text: Stir the schmand smooth with the flour, mix in some hot sauce, then add it all to the pot. Bring briefly to a boil.
steps.label: Thicken sauce

steps.text: Warm the spätzle in a little water and serve with the chicken paprikash.

title: Sheet-Pan Harissa Chicken
summary: Spicy harissa chicken with chickpeas, sweet potato and lemon yogurt. All on one tray.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C (fan). Stir the harissa with the honey, oil and salt.
Dice the sweet potato, cut the onion into wedges, rinse the chickpeas and pat well dry. Toss with half the paste.
Rub the chicken with the remaining paste and place skin side up on the vegetables. Roast.
steps.tip: Skin up and uncovered. That makes it crispy and the chickpeas crunchy.
steps.label: Chicken in oven

steps.text: Stir the yogurt with lemon zest, a little juice and salt.
Serve with lemon yogurt and cilantro.

title: Chicken Saltimbocca
summary: Thin chicken cutlets with sage and Parma ham in a white wine butter sauce.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Halve the chicken breasts horizontally and pound thin between cling film. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
steps.tip: Go easy on the salt, the ham brings plenty.

steps.text: Place a sage leaf and a slice of ham on each cutlet and press on. Lightly flour the underside.
Heat the oil and half the butter and fry the cutlets ham side first until crispy, then flip.
steps.label: Fry saltimbocca

steps.text: Remove the meat. Deglaze with the wine, reduce and swirl in the remaining cold butter. Season with lemon juice.
steps.label: Reduce sauce

steps.text: Serve the saltimbocca with the sauce and potatoes.

title: Chicken Paillard with Lemon Butter
summary: Paper-thin chicken, seared hot, with lemon herb butter and arugula salad. On the table in 25 minutes.

steps.text: Halve the chicken breasts horizontally and pound between cling film to about 5 mm. Season generously.
steps.tip: Evenly thin is the whole secret: it cooks in 2 minutes and stays juicy.

steps.text: Mash the butter with lemon zest, chopped parsley and grated garlic.
Get 2 tbsp oil very hot in a large pan and sear the chicken briefly on each side until golden.
steps.label: Sear chicken

steps.text: Take the pan off the heat, add the lemon butter and a squeeze of lemon and baste the meat with it.
Dress the arugula and halved tomatoes with the remaining oil, lemon juice and salt and shave over the Parmesan.
Serve the chicken with the butter, salad and baguette.

title: Zurich-Style Sliced Veal with Rösti
summary: Tender sliced meat in creamy mushroom sauce with crispy rösti. The Swiss Sunday classic.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in their skins until only half cooked, let cool, peel and grate coarsely.
steps.tip: Par-boiled, cooled potatoes are the Swiss trick for rösti that holds together.
steps.label: Par-boil potatoes

steps.text: Salt the potatoes, press into a flat cake in 2 tbsp clarified butter and fry over medium heat until golden.
steps.label: Rösti side 1

steps.text: Flip the rösti with a plate and fry the second side until crispy.
steps.label: Rösti side 2

steps.text: Cut the meat into thin strips, dust lightly with flour and sear briefly in batches in the remaining clarified butter. Remove.
steps.tip: Sear only briefly! The meat finishes in the sauce and stays tender.
steps.label: Sear meat

steps.text: Fry the shallots and mushrooms in the pan fat, deglaze with the wine, add the stock and cream and reduce until creamy.
steps.label: Reduce sauce

steps.text: Warm the meat briefly in the sauce and season with lemon juice, salt and pepper. Serve with the rösti and parsley.

title: Currywurst with Oven Fries
summary: Berlin's cult snack at home: bratwurst with homemade curry ketchup and crispy oven fries.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C (fan). Cut the potatoes into sticks, soak in water and pat very dry.
steps.tip: Soaking rinses off starch. That's how oven fries get properly crispy instead of limp.
steps.label: Soak fries

steps.text: Toss the fries with 3 tbsp oil and salt, spread in a single layer on the tray and bake, turning halfway.
steps.label: Bake fries

steps.text: Finely dice the onion and sweat in the remaining oil. Briefly toast the tomato paste, curry and paprika.
steps.label: Sweat onion

steps.text: Add the passata, vinegar, honey and 50 ml water, simmer and blend smooth. Season with salt.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Fry the sausages in a pan until browned all over.
steps.label: Fry sausages

steps.text: Slice the sausages, pour over the sauce, dust with curry powder and serve with the fries.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
summary: Sichuan classic with chicken, peanuts, dried chilies and a sweet and tangy sauce.

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the water and let it steam covered.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Dice the chicken and marinate with 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp cornstarch.
steps.tip: The cornstarch coats the meat like a jacket and keeps it juicy over high heat.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.text: Stir the remaining soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, remaining cornstarch and 3 tbsp water. Dice the pepper, cut the spring onions into pieces and slice the garlic and ginger.
Heat the oil in a wok, briefly toast the chilies and Sichuan pepper, then add the chicken and fry until cooked.
steps.label: Fry chicken

steps.text: Briefly fry the pepper, garlic, ginger and spring onions. Pour in the sauce until glossy and fold in the peanuts.
steps.label: Glaze

steps.text: Serve with rice.

title: Sweet and Sour Chicken
summary: Crispy fried chicken with pineapple and peppers in a glossy sweet and sour sauce.

steps.text: Bring the rice to a boil with twice the water and some salt and let it steam covered.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Dice the chicken, salt it and coat first in beaten egg, then in 4 tbsp cornstarch.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the chicken in batches until crispy all over. Remove.
steps.tip: Egg and cornstarch give the typical crispy coating like at a Chinese takeaway.
steps.label: Fry chicken

steps.text: Stir the pineapple juice with the ketchup, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar and remaining cornstarch.
Cut the peppers and onion into pieces and fry briefly in the pan fat. Add the garlic and pineapple, pour in the sauce and boil until glossy.
steps.label: Veg & sauce

steps.text: Fold in the chicken and serve right away with rice.
steps.tip: Fold it in only at the very end, or the crust goes soft.

title: Oyakodon
summary: Japanese rice bowl with chicken and silky egg in a sweet dashi sauce. Ready in 25 minutes.

steps.text: Rinse the rice and bring to a boil with 200 ml water, then let it steam covered.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Cut the onion into strips and the chicken into small pieces.
Bring the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar to a boil in a small pan and cook the onion and chicken in it.
steps.label: Cook chicken

steps.text: Beat the eggs only very loosely, pour over the chicken, cover and cook until half set.
steps.tip: Beat only briefly so the white and yolk are still visible. That gives the typical silky texture.
steps.label: Set egg

steps.text: Put the rice in bowls, slide the chicken and egg with the sauce over the top and sprinkle with spring onions.

title: Bulgogi Bowl
summary: Korean beef marinated with pear, soy sauce and sesame, seared hot over rice.

steps.text: Freeze the beef briefly, then slice paper-thin.
steps.tip: 20 minutes in the freezer firms up the meat so you can slice it paper-thin.
steps.label: Chill beef

steps.text: Grate the pear and mix with the soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, grated garlic and ginger. Marinate the beef in it.
steps.tip: The pear contains enzymes that tenderize the meat. An old Korean trick!
steps.label: Marinate

steps.text: Rinse the rice, bring to a boil with 200 ml water and let it steam covered.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Thinly slice the cucumber and toss with the vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Get the oil very hot in a pan and sear the beef in batches until caramelized.
steps.label: Sear beef

steps.text: Plate with rice, cucumber and kimchi and sprinkle with spring onions and sesame.

title: Tonkatsu with Cabbage Slaw
summary: Japanese pork cutlet with a super crispy panko crust, cabbage slaw and tonkatsu sauce.

steps.text: Rinse the rice, bring to a boil with 200 ml water and let it steam covered.
steps.label: Rice

steps.text: Shave the cabbage paper-thin and put it in ice water.
steps.tip: Ice water makes the cabbage extra crunchy, just like in a Japanese restaurant.

steps.text: Nick the fat edge of the pork, pound lightly, season and coat in flour, egg and panko.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 170 °C and fry the cutlets until golden, turning once.
steps.label: Fry tonkatsu

steps.text: Drain on a rack and rest for 2 minutes. Stir the ketchup, Worcestershire and soy sauce together.
steps.label: Let rest

steps.text: Slice into strips and serve with the drained cabbage, lemon, rice and sauce.

title: Chicken Fajitas
summary: Spicy marinated chicken with peppers and onions, sizzling hot in tortillas.

steps.text: Cut the chicken into strips and marinate with the spices, grated garlic, juice of one lime, 1 tbsp oil and salt.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.text: Cut the peppers and onion into strips. Mash the avocado with lime juice and salt.
Get the remaining oil very hot in a cast-iron pan and sear the chicken. Remove.
steps.tip: Really hot! The sizzle and the charred spots are what make real fajitas.
steps.label: Sear chicken

steps.text: Fry the peppers and onion in the same pan until crisp-tender, then return the chicken.
steps.label: Fry vegetables

steps.text: Warm the tortillas and fill with the fajita mix, guacamole, sour cream and cilantro.

title: Köfte with Bulgur and Yogurt
summary: Turkish meatballs with cumin and parsley, with tomato bulgur and garlic yogurt.

steps.text: Finely grate the onion and squeeze out the juice. Knead vigorously with the mince, chopped parsley, cumin, Aleppo pepper, salt and pepper.
steps.tip: Knead for a long time until the mixture turns sticky. That's how köfte hold together and stay juicy.

steps.text: Shape into small oblong patties and chill.
steps.label: Chill

steps.text: Toast the tomato paste in 1 tbsp oil, add the bulgur and diced tomatoes, pour in hot stock and let it swell covered.
steps.label: Soak bulgur

steps.text: Stir the yogurt with grated garlic and salt.
Fry the köfte and peppers in a grill pan with the remaining oil all over.
steps.label: Fry köfte

steps.text: Serve with the bulgur, peppers and garlic yogurt.

title: Ćevapčići with Ajvar
summary: Balkan grilled mince rolls with ajvar, onions and djuvec rice.

steps.text: Knead the mince for a long time with 2 grated garlic cloves, paprika, baking soda, 3 tbsp water, salt and pepper.
steps.tip: A pinch of baking soda is the Balkan trick: the ćevapčići turn tender and juicy.

steps.text: Shape finger-length rolls and chill.
steps.label: Chill

steps.text: Dice one onion and the pepper and sweat in the oil. Briefly toast the remaining garlic, tomato paste and rice.
steps.label: Sweat vegetables

steps.text: Pour in the stock, add the peas and let it swell covered.
steps.label: Djuvec rice

steps.text: Fry the ćevapčići in a grill pan or on the grill until browned all over.
steps.label: Grill ćevapčići

steps.text: Finely dice the second onion. Serve the ćevapčići with the rice, ajvar, raw onion and parsley.

title: Steak with Herb Butter and Roast Potatoes
summary: Perfectly cooked steak using the reverse-sear method, with herb butter and rosemary potatoes.

steps.text: Salt the steaks generously and leave them uncovered in the fridge, ideally from the day before.
steps.tip: Dry-salting gives the steak a far better crust.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 120 °C. Halve the potatoes, toss with 2 tbsp oil, rosemary and salt and put them on a tray. Place the steaks on a rack above.
steps.tip: Reverse sear: gently in the oven first, then a quick hard sear in the pan. That makes it pink from edge to edge.

steps.text: Cook the steaks in the oven until about 50 °C inside (medium rare). Then remove them and turn the oven up to 220 °C for the potatoes.
steps.label: Steaks in oven

steps.text: Mash the butter with chopped parsley, grated garlic and salt. Finish roasting the potatoes until crispy.
steps.label: Roast potatoes

steps.text: Get the remaining oil smoking hot in a pan and sear the steaks briefly on each side.
steps.label: Sear steaks

steps.text: Serve with pepper, herb butter, the potatoes and lamb's lettuce with balsamic.

title: Bucatini all'Amatriciana
summary: Roman classic with crispy guanciale, tomatoes, chili and pecorino.

steps.text: Put on water for the pasta and salt lightly. Cut the guanciale into strips.
Render the guanciale slowly in a cold pan until crispy. Pour off half the fat.
steps.tip: Real amatriciana has no onion or garlic. The pork fat carries the flavor.
steps.label: Render guanciale

steps.text: Deglaze with the wine, add the chili and crushed tomatoes and simmer.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Cook the pasta until al dente.
steps.label: Cook pasta

steps.text: Add the pasta with a little pasta water to the sauce, toss and stir in half the pecorino off the heat.
Serve with the remaining pecorino and pepper.

title: Grandma's Chicken Soup
summary: Clear, rich broth with tender chicken, vegetables and noodles. Warms you from the inside.

steps.text: Put the chicken in a pot with 2 liters of cold water, the halved unpeeled onion, bay leaves and peppercorns and bring slowly to a boil.
steps.tip: Starting cold draws more flavor from the meat. The onion skin gives the broth its golden color.

steps.text: Skim off the foam and let the broth simmer very gently on the lowest heat. Don't let it boil hard.
steps.tip: A rolling boil makes the broth cloudy.
steps.label: Simmer broth

steps.text: Trim the vegetables and cut into small cubes or rings.
Take out the chicken and strain the broth. Cook the vegetables in the broth.
steps.label: Cook vegetables

steps.text: Add the noodles. Pull the meat off the bones and return it to the pot.
steps.label: Cook noodles

steps.text: Season well with salt and serve with chopped parsley.

title: Goulash Soup
summary: Spicy, hearty soup with beef, peppers and potatoes. The mountain hut classic.

steps.text: Cut the meat into small cubes, roughly dice the onions.
Brown the meat well in hot oil in batches, then remove. Cook the onions in the fat until golden.
steps.tip: Lots of onions, browned for a long time: they melt away later and make the soup thick.
steps.label: Brown onions

steps.text: Briefly toast the tomato paste. Stir in the paprika only for a moment, then immediately deglaze with stock.
steps.tip: Paprika burns quickly and turns bitter.

steps.text: Add the meat, garlic, caraway and marjoram and braise covered.
steps.label: Braise

steps.text: Dice the potatoes and pepper, add them and simmer until everything is tender.
steps.label: Cook potatoes

steps.text: Season with salt and serve with bread.

title: Boeuf Bourguignon
summary: Beef slowly braised in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and pearl onions. France's Sunday dinner.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 160 °C (320 °F). Cut the meat into large cubes and pat very dry.
steps.tip: Wet meat steams instead of browning. The most important rule for this dish.

steps.text: Dice the bacon and render it in a Dutch oven. Brown the meat in batches in the fat until dark on all sides.
steps.label: Brown meat

steps.text: Roughly chop the carrots and onion and brown them. Briefly toast the tomato paste and flour.
steps.label: Brown vegetables

steps.text: Return the meat, pour in the wine and stock, add the garlic, thyme and bay. Braise covered in the oven.
steps.tip: Use a wine you'd also drink. The rest of the bottle goes with dinner.
steps.label: Braise in oven

steps.text: Shortly before the end, fry the mushrooms and peeled pearl onions in butter until golden.
steps.label: Fry mushrooms

steps.text: Fold in the mushrooms and onions and season. Serve with baguette or mashed potatoes.

title: Quiche Lorraine
summary: Buttery crust, creamy custard and plenty of bacon. The original from Lorraine, no cheese needed.

steps.text: Quickly knead the flour, cold diced butter, 1 egg, a pinch of salt and 2 tbsp cold water into a dough and chill.
steps.tip: Cold hands, cold butter, brief kneading: that makes the crust short instead of tough.
steps.label: Chill dough

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (390 °F). Roll out the dough, line a tart pan and prick with a fork. Blind bake.
steps.tip: Weigh it down with parchment and dried beans, otherwise the crust puffs up.
steps.label: Blind bake

steps.text: Cut the bacon into strips and fry until crispy. Whisk the remaining eggs with the cream, milk, nutmeg and pepper.
Spread the bacon on the crust and pour over the custard. Bake at 180 °C (355 °F) until the center is just set.
steps.label: Bake quiche

steps.text: Let it cool a little and serve warm with a green salad.

title: French Onion Soup
summary: Deeply caramelized onions in rich stock, topped with cheesy toast. A Paris bistro classic.

steps.text: Slice the onions into thin half-moons.
Caramelize the onions in butter with a little salt over medium-low heat until deep golden brown, stirring often.
steps.tip: No shortcut: the color of the onions is the flavor of the soup. Loosen stuck bits with a splash of water.
steps.label: Caramelize onions

steps.text: Briefly toast the flour, deglaze with the wine, then add the stock and thyme and simmer.
steps.label: Simmer soup

steps.text: Slice and toast the baguette. Ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls, top with bread and sprinkle with cheese.
Broil until the cheese bubbles and browns.
steps.label: Broil

title: Matjes Herring Hausfrau Style
summary: Tender matjes herring in cream sauce with apple, onion and pickle, with boiled potatoes. A northern German summer.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Cut the apple, onion and pickles into thin strips. Stir with the sour cream, yogurt, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
steps.tip: A splash of pickle brine in the sauce adds the classic fresh tang.

steps.text: Cut the herring into bite-sized pieces and fold in. Let it marinate briefly.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.text: Sprinkle with plenty of dill and serve with the potatoes.

title: Swabian Maultaschen with Onions
summary: Swabian filled pasta pockets, pan-fried in butter with crispy onions and egg. With potato salad.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in their skins.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Peel and slice the potatoes and mix with the hot stock, vinegar, mustard, oil, salt and pepper. Let it sit.
steps.tip: Swabian potato salad should be a little creamy: the warm stock soaks into the potatoes.

steps.text: Cut the Maultaschen into strips. Slice the onion into rings and fry in butter until golden.
steps.label: Fry onions

steps.text: Add the Maultaschen and brown on both sides. Whisk the eggs, pour over and let them set.
steps.label: Brown

steps.text: Sprinkle with chives and serve with the potato salad.

title: Bavarian Roast Pork with Crackling
summary: Bavarian Sunday roast with crispy crackling and dark beer gravy. With dumplings and cabbage.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (355 °F). Score the rind in a diamond pattern without cutting into the meat. Rub the meat with salt, caraway, mustard and garlic.
steps.tip: A box cutter makes scoring the rind much easier.

steps.text: Place the roast rind side down in a roasting pan with 2 cm of water and cook.
steps.tip: This softens the rind so it can puff up perfectly later.
steps.label: Soften rind

steps.text: Turn over, add the roughly chopped vegetables and gradually pour in the beer and stock. Baste the roast often, but not the rind.
steps.label: Roast

steps.text: Switch the oven to 220 °C (430 °F) grill and let the crackling puff up. Keep a close eye on it.
steps.label: Crackling

steps.text: Strain the gravy, pressing the vegetables through, and season. Heat the dumplings and red cabbage as directed.
Slice the roast and serve with gravy, dumplings and red cabbage.

title: Kassler with Sauerkraut
summary: Tender cured smoked pork on wine sauerkraut with apple, with mashed potatoes. Wintry and easy.

steps.text: Dice the onion and sweat it in some butter. Grate the apple and cook briefly.
steps.label: Sweat onions

steps.text: Add the sauerkraut, wine, juniper and bay. Lay the Kassler on top and cook gently, covered.
steps.tip: Don't rinse the sauerkraut, or you'll lose flavor and vitamins.
steps.label: Cook Kassler

steps.text: Peel the potatoes and boil in salted water until soft.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Drain and mash the potatoes. Stir in warm milk, the remaining butter, salt and nutmeg.
steps.tip: Never use a stick blender, it makes the mash gluey.

steps.text: Serve the Kassler with sauerkraut and mash.

title: Hamburg Pan-Fried Fish
summary: Pan-fried fish with fried potatoes and mustard sauce. The Hamburg fishermen's dish.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in their skins, let them cool and slice.
steps.tip: Day-old potatoes are perfect: cold potatoes get the crispiest.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Fry the potatoes in oil until crispy, adding the diced onion toward the end.
steps.label: Fried potatoes

steps.text: Bring the stock and cream to a boil, stir in both mustards and reduce slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
steps.tip: Stir in the mustard last and don't boil it again, or it gets bitter.
steps.label: Mustard sauce

steps.text: Cut the fish into pieces, salt, dredge in flour and fry in butter until golden.
steps.label: Fry fish

steps.text: Arrange everything in the pan, spoon the sauce over and sprinkle with dill.

title: Trout Meunière
summary: Whole trout in brown butter with lemon and parsley, with boiled potatoes. Simple and perfect.

steps.text: Peel the potatoes and boil in salted water until tender.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Pat the trout dry inside and out, season with salt and pepper and dredge in flour. Tap off excess flour.
Fry in oil and a knob of butter over medium heat on the first side.
steps.tip: The trout is done when the dorsal fin pulls out easily.
steps.label: First side

steps.text: Carefully turn and fry the second side.
steps.label: Second side

steps.text: Remove the fish. Add the remaining butter to the pan, let it foam until nutty brown, then add lemon juice and parsley.
Pour the butter over the trout and serve with the potatoes.

title: Gambas al Ajillo (Garlic Prawns)
summary: Prawns in sizzling garlic oil with chili. Spain's favorite tapa, with bread for dipping.

steps.text: Thaw the prawns and pat them very dry, salt lightly. Thinly slice the garlic, cut the chili into rings.
Heat the olive oil slowly with the garlic and chili until the garlic just turns pale golden.
steps.tip: Start in cold oil: the garlic releases its flavor without burning.
steps.label: Garlic in oil

steps.text: Turn up the heat, add the prawns and cook until just pink. Add the sherry and paprika.
steps.label: Cook prawns

steps.text: Sprinkle with parsley and serve sizzling with bread.

title: Shrimp Scampi Pasta
summary: Linguine with shrimp in garlic white wine butter and lemon. On the table in 20 minutes.

steps.text: Cook the linguine in well-salted water until al dente. Save a cup of pasta water.
steps.label: Cook pasta

steps.text: Sear the shrimp briefly in olive oil and remove.
steps.tip: Better too short than too long: the shrimp finish cooking in the sauce.
steps.label: Sear shrimp

steps.text: Sweat the garlic and chili flakes in half the butter, deglaze with wine and reduce by half.
steps.label: Reduce wine

steps.text: Add the pasta, shrimp, remaining butter, lemon juice and zest and some pasta water and toss until the sauce is glossy.
Serve with plenty of parsley.

title: Mussels in White Wine
summary: Mussels steamed in white wine, shallots and garlic, with baguette for the broth. Fresh from September!

steps.text: Scrub the mussels thoroughly and pull off the beards. Discard any open mussels that don't close when tapped.
steps.tip: Mussel season is the months with an "r": September to April.

steps.text: Finely chop the shallots and garlic and sweat in butter.
steps.label: Sweat shallots

steps.text: Pour in the wine, bring to a boil, add the mussels and steam covered. Shake the pot now and then.
steps.label: Steam mussels

steps.text: Discard any mussels that stayed closed. Stir the cream, pepper and parsley into the broth.
Serve in the pot with baguette for dipping.

title: Spaghetti alle Vongole
summary: Spaghetti with clams, garlic, white wine and parsley. The favorite dish on the Bay of Naples.

steps.text: Soak the clams in cold salted water so they spit out any sand, then rinse.
steps.label: Soak clams

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti in salted water 2 minutes less than the package says.
steps.label: Cook pasta

steps.text: Gently sweat the garlic and chili in olive oil, add the clams and wine and cook covered until they open.
steps.label: Cook clams

steps.text: Add the spaghetti and some pasta water to the pan and finish cooking in the clam juice until it turns silky.
steps.tip: In Naples there's no Parmesan on vongole. Parsley and a drizzle of good oil are enough.
steps.label: Finish pasta

steps.text: Serve with parsley and a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Lasagna Bolognese
summary: Layers of slow-cooked ragù, béchamel and Parmesan. The ultimate family meal.

steps.text: Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery and sweat in olive oil until soft.
steps.label: Soffritto

steps.text: Add the mince and fry until crumbly and browned. Toast the tomato paste, then deglaze with wine.
steps.label: Brown mince

steps.text: Add the tomatoes and 250 ml milk and simmer the ragù uncovered on low heat.
steps.tip: Milk in the ragù is the original Bolognese way: it makes the meat tender and mellow.
steps.label: Simmer ragù

steps.text: For the béchamel, melt the butter, stir in the flour, gradually whisk in the remaining milk and let it thicken. Season with salt and nutmeg.
steps.label: Béchamel

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (355 °F). Layer ragù, sheets, béchamel and Parmesan, finishing with béchamel and Parmesan. Bake.
steps.label: Bake lasagna

steps.text: Let it rest before cutting so the layers hold.
steps.tip: Reheated the next day, lasagna tastes even better.
steps.label: Rest

title: Spaghetti and Meatballs
summary: Juicy meatballs in tomato sauce over spaghetti. A Little Italy classic.

steps.text: Remove the crusts and soak the bread in milk. Knead with the mince, egg, half the Parmesan, 1 grated garlic clove, salt and pepper.
steps.tip: The soaked bread is the secret to juicy, tender meatballs.

steps.text: Shape walnut-sized balls and brown them all over in olive oil.
steps.label: Brown meatballs

steps.text: Add the remaining garlic, stir in the tomatoes and oregano and simmer the meatballs in the sauce.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti in salted water until al dente.
steps.label: Cook pasta

steps.text: Plate the spaghetti with sauce and meatballs and top with basil and the remaining Parmesan.

title: Juicy Meatloaf
summary: Savory meatloaf with a glossy glaze, served with mashed potatoes. Cozy Sunday food.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (355 °F). Soak and squeeze out the roll. Finely dice the onion and sweat it.
steps.tip: Sautéed instead of raw onions make the loaf milder and juicier.
steps.label: Sweat onions

steps.text: Knead the mince with the roll, onion, egg, parsley, mustard, paprika, salt and pepper and shape into a loaf.
Bake the meatloaf on a tray.
steps.label: Bake meatloaf

steps.text: Stir the ketchup and honey together, brush over the loaf and bake until the glaze is glossy.
steps.label: Glaze

steps.text: Boil the potatoes, mash with warm milk and butter and salt.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Let the meatloaf rest briefly, slice and serve with the mash.

title: Toast Hawaii
summary: Toast with ham, pineapple and melted cheese. The cult 1950s German snack, quick and tasty.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C (430 °F) grill. Spread the toast thinly with butter.
Top with ham, well-drained pineapple and cheese.
steps.tip: Pat the pineapple dry, otherwise the toast gets soggy.

steps.text: Bake until the cheese melts and bubbles.
steps.label: Bake

steps.text: Dust with paprika and serve hot.

title: Bacon-Wrapped Pork Tenderloin
summary: Tender pork tenderloin wrapped in crispy bacon with creamy mushrooms. Festive but easy.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 180 °C (355 °F). Trim the sinew from the tenderloin, season with pepper and wrap tightly with bacon.
steps.tip: Barely salt it: the bacon brings enough salt.

steps.text: Sear the tenderloin all over in oil until the bacon colors.
steps.label: Sear

steps.text: Roast in the oven until still slightly pink inside (60 °C / 140 °F core temperature).
steps.label: Roast tenderloin

steps.text: Cook the tagliatelle in salted water.
steps.label: Cook pasta

steps.text: Slice the mushrooms and fry in the pan fat with the shallot and thyme. Add the cream and reduce.
steps.label: Creamy mushrooms

steps.text: Let the tenderloin rest briefly, slice and serve with the noodles and creamy mushrooms.

title: Orecchiette with Broccoli
summary: Broccoli cooked with the pasta until it falls apart into a creamy sauce. With chili and garlic.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it generously.
Cut the broccoli into small florets, peel the stalk and dice it finely. Slice the garlic.
steps.tip: The stalk is the best part: peeled, it's sweet and tender.

steps.text: Add the pasta and broccoli to the boiling water together.
steps.label: Pasta & broccoli

steps.text: Meanwhile, gently heat the olive oil with garlic and chili in a large pan until the garlic is lightly golden.
Save a cup of pasta water. Drain the pasta and broccoli, add to the pan and stir hard with a splash of pasta water until the broccoli breaks down.
steps.tip: Feel free to mash it a bit with the spoon. The more the broccoli breaks down, the creamier it gets.

steps.text: Sprinkle with Parmesan and serve right away.

title: Pasta alla Gricia
summary: The Roman mother of carbonara and amatriciana: guanciale, pecorino, pepper. Nothing else needed.

steps.text: Bring a pot of water to a boil, but salt it only lightly.
steps.tip: Guanciale and pecorino are already salty. The pasta water ends up in the sauce later.

steps.text: Cut the guanciale into strips and render slowly in a cold pan until crispy.
steps.label: Render guanciale

steps.text: Add the rigatoni to the water and cook 2 minutes less than the package says.
steps.label: Cook rigatoni

steps.text: Finely grate the pecorino. Coarsely crush the pepper and toast it briefly in the guanciale fat.
Add the pasta and a ladle of pasta water to the pan and finish cooking until the water has almost evaporated.
steps.label: Finish cooking

steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and stir in the pecorino bit by bit with a splash of pasta water until you get a glossy sauce.
steps.tip: Never on the hot burner! Otherwise the cheese clumps.

title: Spaghetti al Pomodoro
summary: Fresh tomatoes, garlic, basil. The dish every Italian kitchen gets judged by.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it generously.
Score the tomatoes with a cross, drop into the boiling water for 30 seconds, peel and chop roughly.
steps.tip: In summer, use ripe field tomatoes. In winter, a can of good peeled tomatoes is better.

steps.text: Crush the garlic and fry gently in the olive oil. Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt and let them cook down.
steps.label: Reduce sauce

steps.text: Add the spaghetti to the water and cook al dente.
steps.label: Cook spaghetti

steps.text: Remove the garlic. Toss the spaghetti in the sauce with a splash of pasta water.
Tear in the basil, drizzle with raw olive oil and serve with Parmesan.
steps.tip: Never cook the basil, or it loses its aroma.

title: Pasta e Fagioli
summary: Thick bean and pasta soup from Italian peasant cooking. Creamy, warming, cheap.

steps.text: Dice the onion, carrot and celery very finely, chop the garlic.
Sweat slowly in the olive oil until soft. Briefly fry the garlic, rosemary and tomato paste with it.
steps.label: Sweat vegetables

steps.text: Add the beans with their liquid and the stock. Take out a third of the beans, purée them and return to the pot.
steps.tip: The puréed beans make the soup creamy without any cream.

steps.text: Cook the pasta right in the soup, stirring often.
steps.label: Pasta in soup

steps.text: Remove the rosemary, season and serve with Parmesan and olive oil.
steps.tip: Simmering a Parmesan rind in it adds huge depth.

title: Risotto alla Milanese
summary: Golden saffron risotto, stirred creamy with butter and Parmesan.

steps.text: Heat the stock and keep it warm. Soak the saffron in a ladle of stock. Finely chop the shallot.
Sweat the shallot in half the butter. Add the rice and stir until the grains turn translucent.
steps.label: Toast rice

steps.text: Deglaze with the wine and let it evaporate. Then add stock one ladle at a time, stirring often.
steps.tip: Only add more when the rice has almost absorbed the stock.
steps.label: Stir risotto

steps.text: Halfway through, stir in the saffron liquid.
Take off the heat and beat in the remaining cold butter and the Parmesan. Rest for 2 minutes.
steps.tip: This vigorous beating is called mantecatura. It makes the risotto flow like lava.

title: Pumpkin Risotto
summary: Creamy risotto with Hokkaido pumpkin, sage and Parmesan. Autumn on a plate.

steps.text: Seed the pumpkin and dice it small, chop the shallot. Heat the stock.
Sweat half the pumpkin with the shallot in a little butter until soft and mash with a fork.
steps.tip: The mashed pumpkin turns the risotto orange and makes it extra creamy.
steps.label: Sweat pumpkin

steps.text: Add the rice, stir until translucent, deglaze with wine. Add the remaining pumpkin and the stock ladle by ladle.
steps.label: Stir risotto

steps.text: Fry the sage leaves in 20 g butter until crispy.
Take the risotto off the heat, stir in the Parmesan and remaining butter. Drizzle with the sage butter.

title: Risi e Bisi
summary: Venetian spring rice with peas, half soup, half risotto.

steps.text: Finely chop the shallot, heat the stock.
Sweat the shallot in butter, briefly sweat half the peas with it.
Add the rice, stir until translucent, then add stock and cook, stirring now and then.
steps.label: Cook rice

steps.text: Add the remaining peas and cook 3 more minutes. It should stay rather soupy.
steps.tip: In Venice it's eaten with a spoon. Better too loose than too firm.
steps.label: Cook peas

steps.text: Finish with butter, Parmesan and parsley.

title: Gnocchi with Mushrooms and Thyme
summary: Crispy pan-fried gnocchi with mushrooms, thyme and Parmesan, all in one pan.

steps.text: Slice the mushrooms, chop the garlic.
Fry the uncooked gnocchi in olive oil until golden all over. Remove.
steps.tip: Don't boil them! Fried straight from the pack they get crispy outside and soft inside.
steps.label: Fry gnocchi

steps.text: Sear the mushrooms in the hot pan without stirring, then add butter, garlic and thyme.
steps.label: Fry mushrooms

steps.text: Return the gnocchi to the pan, season and serve with Parmesan.

title: Pumpkin Lasagna with Sage
summary: Layers of roasted pumpkin, ricotta, béchamel and sage. An autumn Sunday dinner.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (390 °F). Peel and dice the squash, roast on a tray with olive oil and salt.
steps.label: Roast squash

steps.text: For the béchamel, melt the butter, stir in the flour, whisk in the milk gradually and simmer until thick. Season with nutmeg and salt.
steps.label: Béchamel

steps.text: Roughly mash the roasted squash, mix with ricotta and chopped sage.
Layer béchamel, sheets and squash mixture in a dish. Finish with béchamel and Parmesan.
Bake until golden on top.
steps.label: Bake lasagna

steps.text: Rest for 15 minutes, then cut.
steps.tip: Resting is a must. Otherwise it all slides apart.

title: Penne all'Arrabbiata
summary: Tomatoes, garlic, plenty of chili. The angry pasta from Rome.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it generously.
Slice the garlic and fry gently with the chili flakes in olive oil.
steps.tip: Toasting the chili in oil spreads the heat evenly through the whole sauce.

steps.text: Crush the tomatoes by hand, add them, salt and simmer.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Cook the penne al dente.
steps.label: Cook penne

steps.text: Toss the penne in the sauce with a splash of pasta water and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Tagliatelle with Creamy Mushrooms
summary: Ribbon pasta in a creamy sauce of seared mushrooms, white wine and parsley.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it generously.
Clean the mushrooms and cut into pieces. Finely chop the shallot and garlic.
Sear the mushrooms in two batches in hot oil, salt only afterwards.
steps.tip: Too many mushrooms at once stew in their own juice. Fry them in batches.
steps.label: Fry mushrooms

steps.text: Cook the tagliatelle.
steps.label: Cook tagliatelle

steps.text: Add butter, shallot and garlic to the mushrooms, deglaze with wine, pour in the cream and reduce briefly.
steps.label: Reduce sauce

steps.text: Toss the pasta in the sauce, serve with parsley and Parmesan.

title: Pasta with Zucchini, Lemon and Mint
summary: Slowly cooked zucchini that almost turn into a sauce. Fresh with lemon and mint.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it generously.
Coarsely grate the zucchini, finely chop the garlic.
Cook the zucchini with garlic and olive oil over medium heat until soft and lightly golden.
steps.tip: Patience: the longer they cook, the sweeter and creamier they get.
steps.label: Cook zucchini

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti.
steps.label: Cook spaghetti

steps.text: Toss the spaghetti with a splash of pasta water, lemon zest, the juice of half a lemon and the Parmesan into the zucchini.
Sprinkle with mint and serve.

title: Pasta al Tonno
summary: Tomato sauce with tuna, capers and olives. From the pantry in 20 minutes.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it generously.
Chop the garlic and fry with chili in olive oil. Crush the tomatoes, add and simmer.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Cook the spaghetti.
steps.label: Cook spaghetti

steps.text: Drain the tuna and add it to the sauce with the capers and olives only at the end.
steps.tip: Only warm the tuna briefly, or it turns dry and stringy.

steps.text: Toss the pasta in the sauce and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Pasta with Sausage and Fennel
summary: Spicy Italian sausage, sweet fennel and a touch of cream. Rustic and quick.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it generously.
Slice the fennel thinly, keep the fronds. Squeeze the sausage out of its casing.
Fry the sausage meat in olive oil until browned and crumbly.
steps.label: Fry sausage

steps.text: Add fennel and garlic and fry until soft, deglaze with wine.
steps.label: Fry fennel

steps.text: Cook the rigatoni.
steps.label: Cook rigatoni

steps.text: Add cream and a splash of pasta water to the sausage, toss in the pasta, serve with Parmesan and fennel fronds.
steps.tip: The fennel fronds are an herb in their own right. Don't throw them away!

title: Ossobuco
summary: Braised veal shank in wine and tomato until the meat falls off the bone. With lemon gremolata.

steps.text: Cut the skin around the shanks in a few places, season and dust with flour.
steps.tip: The cuts stop the slices from curling up while searing.

steps.text: Sear well on both sides in butter and oil in a Dutch oven. Remove.
steps.label: Sear

steps.text: Finely dice onion, carrot and celery and sweat in the fat until soft. Deglaze with wine.
Add tomatoes and stock, put the meat back in and braise covered over low heat.
steps.label: Braise

steps.text: For the gremolata, finely chop lemon zest, garlic and parsley together.
Sprinkle the ossobuco with gremolata. Serve with saffron risotto or polenta.
steps.tip: The marrow in the bone is the delicacy. Scoop it out with a small spoon!

title: Vitello Tonnato
summary: Tender, thinly sliced veal under a creamy tuna sauce with capers.

steps.text: Put the meat in a pot with onion, carrot, bay leaf and salt, cover with water and poach gently over low heat.
steps.tip: The water should only shiver, never boil. That keeps the meat pink and juicy.
steps.label: Poach veal

steps.text: Let it cool in the broth, then chill in the fridge until firm.
steps.label: Cool down

steps.text: Blend tuna, anchovies, 1 tbsp capers, mayonnaise, a squeeze of lemon and some broth into a smooth sauce.
Slice the meat paper-thin and arrange on a platter.
Cover with the sauce and scatter over the remaining capers.

title: Caprese with Burrata
summary: Sun-ripe tomatoes, creamy burrata, basil and good olive oil. With bread, a whole dinner.

steps.text: Cut the tomatoes into slices and wedges, spread on a platter and salt them.
steps.tip: Never use tomatoes straight from the fridge! Cold, they taste of nothing.

steps.text: Let them sit 5 minutes to release their juice.
Place the burrata in the middle and tear the basil over it.
Drizzle with olive oil, a few drops of balsamic and pepper. Serve with ciabatta.

title: Tomato Bruschetta
summary: Toasted bread rubbed with garlic, topped with seasoned tomatoes and basil.

steps.text: Seed and dice the tomatoes. Mix with basil, salt, pepper and 2 tbsp olive oil.
steps.tip: Seeding keeps the bread crisp. The seeds and pulp make it soggy.

steps.text: Slice the bread and toast in a pan or oven until golden.
steps.label: Toast bread

steps.text: Rub the warm slices with the halved garlic clove.
Top with the tomatoes just before serving and drizzle with olive oil.

title: Rosemary Focaccia
summary: Fluffy sheet-pan bread with a crispy olive oil crust, rosemary and sea salt. Barely any work, just time.

steps.text: Stir flour, yeast, sugar, salt and 420 ml lukewarm water into a sticky dough. Mix in 2 tbsp olive oil.
steps.tip: No kneading! The dough should stay sticky, time does the work.

steps.text: Let it rise covered. Fold it from the outside in twice with wet hands along the way.
steps.label: Let dough rise

steps.text: Grease a tray with 4 tbsp olive oil, add the dough and spread it out with oiled fingers. Let rise again.
steps.label: Second rise

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 230 °C (445 °F). Press deep dimples with your fingertips, drizzle with oil, top with rosemary and sea salt.
Bake until golden.
steps.label: Bake focaccia

steps.text: Cool briefly and cut into pieces while warm.

title: Creamy Polenta with Mushroom Ragout
summary: Silky polenta with Parmesan, topped with a dark mushroom ragout with thyme.

steps.text: Cut the mushrooms into pieces, chop the shallot and garlic.
Sear the mushrooms in hot oil, add shallot, garlic and thyme, deglaze with red wine and reduce.
steps.label: Mushroom ragout

steps.text: Bring milk and stock to a boil. Whisk in the polenta in a thin stream and let it thicken over low heat.
steps.tip: Whisk it in and you won't get any lumps.
steps.label: Cook polenta

steps.text: Stir butter and Parmesan into the polenta. It should be soft and flowing.
Spoon the polenta onto plates and top with the mushroom ragout.

title: Tiramisu
summary: The Italian classic with mascarpone cream, espresso and cocoa. Best made the day before.

steps.text: Brew the coffee and let it cool.
Separate the eggs. Beat the yolks with sugar until pale and creamy, then stir in the mascarpone.
Whip the egg whites until stiff and fold gently into the cream.
steps.tip: Fold, don't stir. That keeps the air in and the cream fluffy.

steps.text: Dip the ladyfingers very briefly in the coffee and line a dish with them. Spread half the cream on top. Repeat.
steps.tip: One second per side is enough. Otherwise it goes soggy.

steps.text: Chill covered for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight. Dust with cocoa before serving.

title: Panna Cotta with Berries
summary: Wobbly vanilla cream with a fruity berry sauce. Perfect for making ahead.

steps.text: Soak the gelatin in cold water.
steps.tip: Gelatin isn't vegetarian. Agar agar (1/2 tsp) works too, just boil it briefly.

steps.text: Heat the cream with 40 g sugar and the scraped vanilla seeds, without boiling.
Take off the heat, squeeze the gelatin and dissolve it in the cream. Pour into glasses and chill.
Briefly boil the berries with the remaining sugar and a squeeze of lemon, then let cool.
steps.label: Cook berries

steps.text: Once the panna cotta has set (about 4 hours), spoon the berry sauce on top.

title: Pappa al Pomodoro
summary: Tuscan bread and tomato soup. Thick, fragrant and a brilliant way to use up bread.

steps.text: Roughly chop the tomatoes, slice the garlic, tear the bread into chunks.
Gently fry the garlic in 4 tbsp olive oil, add the tomatoes and simmer.
steps.label: Simmer tomatoes

steps.text: Add the bread and stock and keep simmering until the bread falls apart. Stir well.
steps.tip: The staler the bread, the better. Fresh bread turns gluey.
steps.label: Cook bread down

steps.text: Stir in the basil, season and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Serve lukewarm with plenty of olive oil.

title: Pasta al Forno
summary: Baked rigatoni with meat and tomato sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan. A family meal from the oven.

steps.text: Chop onion and garlic, sweat in olive oil. Add the meat and fry until crumbly.
steps.label: Fry meat

steps.text: Add the passata, season and simmer.
steps.label: Simmer sauce

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (390 °F). Cook the rigatoni 3 minutes less than the package says.
steps.tip: The pasta keeps cooking in the oven. Otherwise it turns mushy.
steps.label: Cook rigatoni

steps.text: Mix the pasta with the sauce, basil and half the diced mozzarella and put in a baking dish.
Top with the remaining mozzarella and Parmesan and bake.
steps.label: Bake

title: Ravioli with Sage Butter
summary: Store-bought ravioli with nutty brown butter and crispy sage. 15 minutes of happiness.

steps.text: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil.
Add the ravioli to the simmering water and cook.
steps.tip: Just a simmer. Rapidly boiling water makes ravioli burst.
steps.label: Cook ravioli

steps.text: Foam the butter in a pan until light brown and nutty. Fry the sage leaves in it until crispy.
steps.tip: Brown butter smells like hazelnuts. As soon as it does, take the pan off the heat!

steps.text: Lift the ravioli into the pan with a slotted spoon, toss with a spoonful of pasta water.
Serve with Parmesan, pepper and a little lemon zest.

title: Pasta with Pesto Rosso
summary: Homemade pesto of sun-dried tomatoes, almonds and Parmesan. Intense and sunny.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it generously.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan until fragrant.
steps.label: Toast almonds

steps.text: Drain the tomatoes and blend coarsely with almonds, garlic, Parmesan, chili, basil and the olive oil.
steps.tip: The oil from the tomato jar is full of flavor. Just use it too.

steps.text: Cook the fusilli.
steps.label: Cook fusilli

steps.text: Loosen the pesto with a few spoonfuls of pasta water and toss with the pasta.

title: Scaloppine al Limone
summary: Paper-thin cutlets, quickly seared, in a glossy lemon butter sauce.

steps.text: Pound the cutlets thin between plastic wrap, season and dust very lightly with flour.
Fry in olive oil and a little butter for one minute per side. Remove and keep warm.
steps.tip: Only briefly! Thin meat dries out in seconds.
steps.label: Fry cutlets

steps.text: Deglaze with the wine, add the juice of a lemon and reduce briefly.
Take off the heat and swirl in the remaining cold butter until the sauce thickens. Add parsley.
Turn the cutlets briefly in the sauce and serve with ciabatta.

title: Rhenish Sauerbraten
summary: Beef marinated for days in vinegar and spices, braised until tender, with a sweet and sour gravy.

steps.text: Boil vinegar, wine, 250 ml water, roughly chopped vegetables and spices, then cool. Marinate the meat in it covered in the fridge for 3 to 5 days, turning daily.
steps.tip: The longer it marinates, the more tender and flavorful. Three days is the minimum.

steps.text: Take out the meat, pat it very dry, salt and brown well on all sides in clarified butter.
steps.label: Brown meat

steps.text: Briefly fry the vegetables from the marinade, then deglaze with the strained marinade.
Braise covered over low heat until the meat is tender.
steps.label: Braise

steps.text: Remove the meat. Strain the gravy, stir in crumbled gingerbread and raisins and simmer until thick.
steps.tip: The gingerbread thickens the gravy and brings the signature sweetness and spice.
steps.label: Thicken gravy

steps.text: Slice the meat across the grain. Serve with red cabbage and potato dumplings.

title: Leberkäse with Fried Egg and Potato Salad
summary: Crispy fried Bavarian meatloaf, a fried egg on top and sweet mustard. Bavarian pub happiness.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Finely dice the onion and briefly boil it in the hot stock with vinegar, salt and pepper.
Peel the potatoes, slice while warm and pour the hot stock over. Mix in 2 tbsp oil and let it soak in.
steps.tip: Warm potatoes soak up the stock. That makes the salad silky without any mayo.

steps.text: Fry the leberkäse in a pan on both sides until crispy. Fry the eggs next to it.
steps.label: Fry leberkäse

steps.text: Sprinkle the potato salad with chives and serve everything with sweet mustard.

title: Heaven and Earth
summary: A Rhineland classic: mashed potatoes with apple sauce, fried black pudding and crispy onions.

steps.text: Peel and dice the potatoes, boil in salted water until tender.
steps.label: Boil potatoes

steps.text: Peel and dice the apples, stew with sugar and a splash of water until soft.
steps.label: Stew apples

steps.text: Slice the onion into rings and fry in half the butter until golden.
Cut the black pudding into thick slices and fry briefly on both sides.
steps.tip: Dusted with a little flour, it gets a crust and doesn't fall apart.
steps.label: Fry black pudding
